headline: NBC NIGHTLY NEWS for November 9, 2022, NBC
story_text: [19:00:00] (COMMERCIAL BREAK) LESTER HOLT, NBC NEWS ANCHOR (on camera): Tonight, the Midterm Election cliffhanger. The battle for Congress still too close to call. (voiceover): The Senate and the House still up for grabs after the Democrats held off a red wave. President Biden at the White House today calling it a good day for democracy. In Georgia, the tight Senate race headed to a runoff. In Pennsylvania, John Fetterman defeating Mehmet Oz. And in Florida, a big reelection win for Governor Ron DeSantis setting up a possible 2024 showdown with Donald Trump . And what President Biden said today about his own 2024 plans. Our team across the country with a race is still in play. Also breaking tonight, Nicole strengthening into a hurricane and taking aim at Florida flooding on the coast. Buildings collapsing into the sea, mandatory evacuations ordered, the new track tonight. The potential major setback for Russia ordering a retreat from the key city of Kherson in southern Ukraine. Why Kyiv is skeptical. WNBA star Brittney Griner moved to a penal colony in Russia. How the U.S. is responding. Facebook `s parent company Meta laying off thousands. Why Mark Zuckerberg is slashing jobs on the heels of concept Twitter . And "THOSE WHO SERVE," the veterans answering a new call in the classroom. ANNOUNCER: This is NBC NIGHTLY NEWS with Lester Holt. HOLT (on camera): Good evening, everyone, again, tonight from our election headquarters in New York. It was a good day for democracy, President Biden`s first public reaction to yesterday`s Midterm Elections in which Democrats defied the gravity of broad voter dissatisfaction and history itself to avoid massive losses in that widely-predicted Republican wave. Let me tell you from the start tonight, much of our reporting this evening is framed by what we don`t know and that is which party will control Congress. At this hour, control of the Senate is still up for grabs with some races too close to call, while the Georgia Senate contest is headed toward a December runoff election. And the House still in play for both sides, though Republicans currently lead. But there is broad agreement that these were not the results most expected, an unpopular president faced with a bad economy managing to avoid the fate of his predecessors. The President`s message to voters tonight, I get it. Our team has fanned out again this evening watching the count and the issues that shaped the vote starting tonight with Kristen Welker at the White House. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) KRISTEN WELKER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): 24 hours after ballots were cast, tonight, control of Congress is still up for grabs. President Biden insisting it was a good night for Democrats. JOE BIDEN , PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: While the press and the pundits are predicting a giant red wave, it didn`t happen. WELKER: Republicans who had been hoping to take the House in a red wave now just looking for a win. The GOP still favored to take over but with a smaller margin than expected. REP. KEVIN MCCARTHY (R-CA): We will be in the majority and Nancy Pelosi will be in the minority. WELKER: Much more suspense in the Senate where Republicans still could gain the one seat they need to take control but Democrats could hang on to with NBC News projecting races that are too early to call in Nevada and in Arizona. And in Georgia, the showdown between Democratic senator Raphael Warnock and Republican Herschel Walker , NBC News Now projects will go to a runoff. SEN. RAPHAEL WARNOCK (D-GA): We always knew that this race would be close. HERSCHEL WALKER (R-GA), SENATE CANDIDATE: I`m like Ricky Bobby. I don`t come to lose. WELKER: Democrats` biggest win of the night coming in the critical Pennsylvania Senate race. Democrat John Fetterman , six months after suffering a stroke, defeating Republican Dr. Mehmet Oz. JOHN FETTERMAN (D-PA), SENATE CANDIDATE: We did what we needed to do. WELKER: Republicans with big victories too including Georgia Governor Brian Kemp easily defeating Democrat Stacey Abrams . And in the biggest win of the night, Florida Republican Governor Ron DeSantis winning reelection in a 19- point landslide, sweeping virtually every county in the state, including heavily Latino Miami Dade. GOV. RON DESANTIS (R-FL): We reject woke ideology. We will never ever surrender to the woke mob. Florida is where woke goes to die. WELKER: DeSantis seen as a possible 2024 presidential contender where he could face former President Trump who had a tough night. His endorsed candidates in Ohio and North Carolina won but several of Mr. Trump`s other handpick candidates in key races, including New Hampshire, Michigan, and Pennsylvania all lost. Meanwhile, President Biden was asked what he will do differently with most Americans saying they`re dissatisfied with the state of the country. [19:05:08] BIDEN: Nothing because they`re just finding out what we`re doing. The more they know about what we`re doing, the more support there is. WELKER: And we pressed him about running again. Two-thirds of Americans in exit polls say that they don`t think you should run for reelection. What is your message to them? And how does that factor into your final decision about whether or not to run for reelection? BIDEN: It doesn`t. WELKER: What`s your message to those two-thirds of Americans? BIDEN: Watch me. (END VIDEOTAPE) HOLT: Kristen, the President is likely facing divided government. Did he talk about working with Republicans how it would go? WELKER (on camera): Well, Lester, he did. The President says he`ll call top House Republican Kevin McCarthy tonight and says he`s hoping for bipartisanship on issues like Ukraine. The President also saying he`ll make his decision on running early next year. Lester? HOLT: Kristen Welker at the White House, thanks. That pivotal Senate race in Georgia, as we said, is neck and neck. Gabe Gutierrez is there. And Gabe, what can we expect in this coming run off? GABE GUTIERREZ, NBC NEWS NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT (on camera): Lester, this is what both campaigns and many voters did not want, another month of campaigning. But incumbent Raphael Warnock and challenger Herschel Walker are already fundraising ahead of the runoff now set for December 6. Neither managed to get 50 percent of the vote. But in the governor`s race here, Republican incumbent, Brian Kemp easily won reelection over Democrat Stacey Abrams . And that suggests some Republicans may have split their tickets in the Senate contest and voted for Warnock. Now, back in 2020, this state had to runoffs that tipped the balance of power in the Senate. And based on ad spending back then, it`s possible that we could see upwards of $200 million dollars in TV ads here over the next several weeks. Lester? HOLT: Gabe Gutierrez in Atlanta, thanks. Another key state in play. Arizona remains in flux both in the U.S. Senate race between incumbent Mark Kelly and Republican Blake Masters and in the governor`s race. Vaughn Hillyard is in Phoenix tonight. Vaughn, where do things stand right now? VAUGHN HILLYARD, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT (on camera): Yes, Lester, at least a half a million votes have yet to be counted here in Arizona. And as soon as we may know who wins this race for governor and Senate, may be tomorrow night. Elections officials continue to process and tabulate these mail-in votes. And there`s an important batch of votes that are expected to be released tomorrow. These results are going to be mail ballots that were hand delivered by voters instead of being mailed back. In 2018, these votes, they trended towards Democrats, but in 2020, towards Republicans. Now, one other note that if these margins remain close, this is a situation where if these -- any of these races finish with -- finished within a half a percentage point, that it would trigger an automatic recount under state law that wouldn`t begin until December. Lester? HOLT: All right, Vaughn, thanks very much for that. I want to bring in our political director and moderator of "MEET THE PRESS," Chuck Todd. Chuck, Monday night, you and I stood right here. And we talked about whether polarization could be the guiding factor in the election was it? CHUCK TODD, NBC NEWS POLITICAL DIRECTOR (on camera): Look, I don`t think -- I think it was because I don`t know if campaigns mattered. Let me show you Ohio. Tim Ryan ran up almost a perfect race for a Democrat in Ohio. And yet, it didn`t matter how well his campaign win. Look at this. He basically only performed 1.5 percentage points better than Biden. Essentially, the state reverted to its 2020 partisan norm. Let me take you to Colorado, another example but in the other direction. A Republican running a really good race in Colorado, and it got them all of less than a percentage point better than Donald Trump . The point is, it didn`t matter if it was a blue state or a red state. What the partisan makeup was in 2020 seemed to dictate what the result was in 2022. HOLT: All right, Chuck, thanks. Let me turn to Andrea Mitchell now who`s been looking at the Biden effect. How much credit does the President get for staving off this red wave? ANDREA MITCHELL, NBC NEWS CHIEF WASHINGTON CORRESPONDENT (on camera): Well, Lester, President Biden is touting the stronger than expected results. But our exit polls showed more voters believed his policies were hurting the country than helping. So, can Biden take credit for Democrats overperformance? Another one of our exit polls shows President Biden has less of an impact on voters decisions in this midterms than any other President has had in the last decade. That may explain why despite the President`s low approval ratings, Democrats won in states like Pennsylvania and Michigan and avoided the kind of shellacking President Obama suffered when he lost 63 seats in 2010. This election could be the best Midterm performance for any president`s party in the last 20 years, Lester. HOLT A lot to analyze. Andrea, thanks very much. And even though this election is still full of question marks, it`s already setting the stage for 2024 especially for former President Trump and his potential rivals. Here`s Ali Vitali. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) ALI VITALI, NBC NEWS CAPITOL HILL CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): Technically, it`s still 2022. But politically -- DONALD TRUMP , FORMER PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: Stay tuned. VITALI: -- it`s open season on the 2024 Presidential Race. Launched to the front the Republican PAC Tuesday night, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis -- [19:10:03] GOV. RON DESANTIS (R-FL): Thank you for a historic landslide victory. VITALI: Or as the New York Post front page blared, DeFuture. DESANTIS: We`ve got so much more to do, and I have only begun to fight. VITALI: Supporters in the room chanting for two more years. His decisive win here in Florida drawing attention including from fellow Floridian Donald Trump who had his once ally turned likely rival top of mine this weekend. TRUMP: Trump at 71, Ron DeSanctimonious at 10 percent. VITALI: Trump`s handpick candidates suffering a string of losses Tuesday night. TRUMP : I think if they win, I should get all the credit. And if they lose, I should not be blamed at all. WELKER: Who do you think would be the tougher competitor, Ron DeSantis or former President Trump? And how is that factoring into your decision? BIDEN: It`d be fun to watch them take on each other. VITALI: But it`s not just DeSantis eyeing potential bids. GOV. BRIAN KEMP (R-GA): So, give him a big Georgia welcome. VITALI: Former VP Mike Pence also mulling a run, publishing a book So Help Me God out next week, possibly the same day Trump himself could cement his intentions to run again. TRUMP " I`m going to be making a very big announcement. VITALI: Other former Trump officials like Nikki Haley and Mike Pompeo , Senate allies Ted Cruz and Rick Scott , and governors from Arkansas and South Dakota all talked about as possible 2024 contenders. (END VIDEOTAPE) VITALI (on camera): And Pence releasing the first excerpt from his memoir tonight detailing his harrowing experience at the Capitol on January 6, and underscoring his indelible differences with Donald Trump over that day. Lester? HOLT: Ali Vitali, thank you. And meanwhile, Florida is bracing once again for a hurricane. Dylan Dreyer is here. Dylan, Hurricane Nicole is gaining steam. DYLAN DREYER, NBC NEWS METEOROLOGIST (on camera): Yes, it is a hurricane now as it moves through the Bahamas and will likely maintain that category one status as it moves to the west, right now at 12 miles per hour. And then we are looking for the chance of about eight inches of rain across parts of Florida. And this is going to make landfall tonight into early tomorrow morning. And then it`s going to race across the state of Florida, perhaps making another landfall, as it moves its way towards the Gulf of Mexico and then it takes this rapid turn to the north. It`s going to bring all of this rain up into the Northeast where we could see about three to four inches of rain. However, it`s the storm surge down through Daytona Beach and the Jacksonville and the Fort Pierce, the three to five-foot storm surge that could lead to more beach erosion and also some significant flooding right along the coastline. The only saving grace Lester is that the storm hits during low tide. It`s tomorrow morning`s high tide that we`ll worry about. HOLT: All right, Dylan, thanks very much. Let`s get the view from the ground. We want to head to Florida. That`s where NBC Sam Brock is watching as things turn for the worst. Sam? SAM BROCK, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT (on camera): Lester, good evening. The size of the storm is massive just six weeks after Ian. And while many people saw Ian did its damage on the west side of Florida, here on the East Coast, it caused all kinds of erosion. Just look at this beach and how it`s dwindled, exposing the coastline to a direct hit. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) BROCK (voiceover): Tonight, it`s a state of emergency across nearly 50 Florida counties as ocean waters swell from the Space Coast to Daytona Beach. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: We watched a huge chunk of this backyard just dissolve and fall into the ocean this morning. BROCK: Dramatic images show a public restroom sliding into the ocean in Volusia County, while a couple of hours south, the ground literally crumbling beneath a home on Hutchinson Island as Florida getting slammed by the first November hurricane in almost 40 years. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: I just can`t believe that we`re having a storm in November. BROCK: These restaurant owners taking stock of the situation and considering closing down as plywood adorns the Cocoa Beach Pier along with caution tape. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: We boarded up the house and we have our generator. BROCK: Moms like Margaret Lever are on the move but not leaving the storm zone even after Hurricane Ian delivered some harsh lessons only weeks earlier. Did hurricane and changed the mentality for anyone. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: A little bit, not too much. BROCK: Instead of passengers boarding, airport gates are boarded up and school districts across the state are closing even as far south as Miami and Broward. WAYNE IVEY, SHERIFF, BREVARD COUNTY: You know you and you know your place where you live and where you take refuge. BROCK: This historically rare event -- UNIDENTIFIED MALE: The storms are coming later, storms are coming bigger. BROCK: -- ready to potentially wreak havoc on a state still in recovery mode. Sam Brock, NBC News Jensen Beach, Florida. (END VIDEOTAPE) HOLT: In 60 seconds, the major retreat ordered by Russia in Ukraine, a troubling new turn for basketball superstar Brittney Griner in Russia, and what Mark Zuckerberg just said about cuts at Facebook `s parent company. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [19:15:00] HOLT: We`re back now with a potential major blow to Vladimir Putin`s war effort in Ukraine. After weeks of Ukrainian advances, the Russian military announced it is retreating from Kherson, the first major city that fell after the invasion began in February. Kyiv is skeptical, however, fearing the announcement could be a ruse to lead Ukrainian troops into a trap. And in Russia, WNBA star Brittney Griner has been moved to a penal colony in an undisclosed location according to her attorneys. Griner was sentenced in Russia in August to nine years in prison on drug possession charges. Despite the stalled efforts to free Griner, President Biden said today he is determined to bring her home. MARK ZUCKERBERG , CEO, FACEBOOK : I want to say, you know, upfront that I take full responsibility for this decision. COSTELLO: The CEO of Facebook parent company, Meta , announcing the company would be laying off 11,000 employees, a stunning 13 percent of the workforce, saying the company needs to become leaner and more efficient. ZUCKERBERG: It is one of the hardest calls that I`ve had to make in the 18 years of running the company. COSTELLO: The trouble, Meta ramped up hiring during and after the pandemic while spending billions on Zuckerberg`s vision of a virtual reality future called the Metaverse. But the metaverse may now have to wait Mehta stock is down 70 percent this year, profits down 50 percent in the third quarter. With the economy slowing, Meta is the latest tech companies squeezed by a sharp decline in advertising revenue. JULIA BOORSTIN, CNBC SENIOR MEDIA AND TECH CORRESPONDENT: This is Mark Zuckerberg saying we grew too fast. We assumed that the boom times would continue. COSTELLO: And they haven`t. BOORSTIN: This is a really tough time right now for any ad-supported platform. COSTELLO: Meta employees took to social media of course to vent. "The inevitable has happened to me. I woke up today to news I was being laid off," wrote one. Another wrote, "Gutted, devastated, sobbing all morning." (END VIDEOTAPE) COSTELLO (on camera): Meanwhile, Tesla stock closed near a two year low today after Elon Musk sold nearly $4 billion dollars-worth of stock following his purchase of Twitter . And tonight, President Biden said Musk`s relationship with other countries should be looked into. Lester? HOLT: OK, Tom, thanks. Up next, the issue that turned out to be a game-changer in states red and blue. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [19:20:00] HOLT: In the wake of the Supreme Court overturning Roe v Wade, the Midterm Elections saw a record number of abortion-related measures on the ballot. And in every state where voters had a direct say, they opted against restricting access. Here`s Yamiche Alcindor. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) YAMICHE ALCINDOR, NBC NEWS WASHINGTON CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): Tonight, Democrats across the country are celebrating sweeping wins for supporters of abortion rights. JOSH SHAPIRO (D-PA), GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE: A woman`s right to choose one. SEN. MAGGIE HASSAN (D-NH): I will always, always keep fighting to protect a woman`s fundamental freedom. GOV. GRETCHEN WHITMER (D-MI): We will make Michigan a leader, a place where women make their own decisions. ALCINDOR: In Michigan, residents voted to enshrine abortion rights into the state constitution, an issue Governor Gretchen Whitmer and her running mate been a central part of their successful reelection campaign. WHITMER: This is a right that we are not going to go backwards on. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: I`m proud of my state. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: I don`t want the government in my bedroom. ALCINDOR: And abortion rights did drive people to the polls. It was the second most important issue to voters behind inflation. In addition to Michigan, voters in California and Vermont codified abortion rights into their state constitutions. And it wasn`t just blue states, voters in Kentucky and Montana shot down measures that could have restricted access. What do you make of that nationally? WHITMER: I think it`s a sign that the American public has had rights for 49 years. We`re not going to go backward. And so, whether it`s state by state we see this happen or hopefully at some point, you know, a national effort again, I think that this is where the fight is at the moment. ALCINDOR: Those against abortion rights not processing the results. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: I believe abortion is first-degree murder. ALCINDOR: Eric Scheidler from the Pro-Life Action League says he`s gearing up to continue their push. ERIC SCHEIDLER, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, PRO-LIFE ACTION LEAGUE: If we`ve learned anything over the past 50 years as a movement is that we`ve got to be able to take a punch. ALCINDOR: Still, Americans in five states send a clear message about reproductive rights. Yamiche Alcindor, NBC News, Detroit. (END VIDEOTAPE) HOLT: Coming up, their new mission: training troops to become teachers in "THOSE WHO SERVE." (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) COURTNEY KUBE, NBC NEWS PENTAGON (voiceover): After more than two decades in the Navy, John Altman still wanted to serve. He swapped his years at sea for days in the classroom. JOHN ALTMAN, U.S. VETERAN: I`m on the frontlines of developing America`s number one natural resource. What`s that? I teach high school. KUBE: John discovered a program called Troops To Teachers supporting men and women leaving the military to become educators, providing money, counseling, and job referrals with a focus on science, math, and special education in low-income communities. What is it that you hope that you instill upon your students? ALTMAN: You got to work hard if you want something. That you can google your way through life. KUBE: Life lessons his students at Paradise Valley High School take to heart. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: He`s definitely taught me to get stuff done on time and not put it off. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: People from the military could basically go and do anything and he chose to come be a teacher. KUBE: With a need for teachers -- UNIDENTIFIED MALE: The teacher shortage that you hear about is real. I`m in the trenches trying to find teachers. KUBE: Programs like Troops To Teachers are more critical than ever. ALTMAN: I`m glad I found the program. I think it`s important for me to be an example just as when I wore the uniform. KUBE: For Altman, a new battle rhythm with the same mission. ALTMAN: I think that`s my duty assignment. I believe in that. Where`s my force? These youngsters are our tomorrow. I really love my Navy and I love teaching. KUBE: Courtney Kube, NBC News Paradise Valley, Arizona. (END VIDEOTAPE) HOLT: And that`s NIGHTLY NEWS for this Wednesday. Thank you for watching, everyone. headline: Today for November 9, 2022, NBC
story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:00:17] HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Good Wednesday morning. After an election night of midterm surprises for both parties. SAVANNAH GUTHRIE, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: And we are still awaiting many of the results. It is November 9th. This is Today. Too close to call key races still to be decided control of Congress hanging in the balance as votes are still being counted in key battlegrounds this morning. In Pennsylvania Democrats pick up a hard fought Senate seat. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) JOHN FETTERMAN (D-PA), SENATOR-ELECT: I`ll be the next U.S. senator from Pennsylvania. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: In Florida, Governor Ron DeSantis wins big, grossing back to the State House and turning Florida decidedly red. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) GOV. RON DESANTIS (R-FL): The people have delivered their verdict. Freedom is here to stay. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: But across the country controversial Republican candidates aligned with former President Trump disappoint. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) SEN. LINDSEY GRAHAM (R-SC): Definitely not a Republican way that`s for darn sure. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: This morning suspense over who will control the House and Senate and the results still rolling in today, Wednesday, November 9th, 2022. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: From NBC News, this is a special edition of Today with Savannah Guthrie and Hoda Kotb live from Studio 1A in Rockefeller Plaza. GUTHRIE: Well, hi, everybody. Good morning and welcome to Today. It is nice to have you with us on a Wednesday morning, the morning after election night. KOTB: One, two, three cups of coffee and one more for you, a long night. But election results by the way, SG, still coming in right now. GUTHRIE: Absolutely. Big night for the NBC News team all-nighters but we still have the question that we headed into the night with, will there be a shift in the balance of power in Congress? It`s unknown at this hour so let`s break it down where things stand, 218 seats are needed to claim majority control in the House. And right now our projection for the House is essentially still a tossup. Now let`s go to the Senate, both parties still neck and neck there as well. KOTB: Yes, Democrats have flipped one seat. NBC News projecting Democrat John Fetterman has won his Pennsylvania seat defeating Dr. Mehmet Oz in a closely watched an extremely expensive race. GUTHRIE: Let`s go down to Georgia, neither Democrat Raphael Warnock or Republican Herschel Walker have met the 50 percent threshold yet necessary to be declared an outright winner. So it could be that they will go to a runoff election in December. KOTB: Yes, it`s still too early to call. The Senate battle in Arizona, that`s between incumbent Senator Mark Kelly and Republican Blake Masters. GUTHRIE: And in Nevada it is just after 4:00 a.m. and we`re starting to see some results in the race between the incumbent Senator Catherine Cortez Masto and Republican challenger Adam Laxalt . So put it this way, we get a lot to get to. Our correspondents, they`ve been up all night they are spread out from coast to coast. Let`s get it started with NBC`s Peter Alexander in Philadelphia this morning. Hi, Peter, good morning. PETER ALEXANDER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Savannah and Hoda, good morning to both of you. What a night. The crucial Senate seat here in Pennsylvania was a top target for both parties. But now the Democrats have secured a huge flip with John Fetterman`s win. Historically in a midterm, the party in power loses dozens of seats. But Democrats this go around defied history and expectations. And with plenty of votes still to be counted, this remains a country that is deeply divided. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) ALEXANDER (voice-over): This morning, controlled of Congress up in the air with both the House and Senate still hanging in the balance. Republicans acknowledging the expected red wave never materialized. GRAHAM: Definitely not a Republican wave that`s for darn sure. SEN. TED CRUZ (R-TX): That hasn`t been as big of a wave as I`d hoped it would be. ALEXANDER (voice-over): While the battle for the Senate may not be decided for days, Democrats are celebrating a critical Senate pick up in Pennsylvania, where Lieutenant Governor John Fetterman just months removed from a stroke, defeated his Republican rival, celebrity T.V., Dr. Mehmet Oz. FETTERMAN: Yes, this campaign has always been about fighting for everyone who`s ever been gotten knocked down that ever got back up. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Georgia`s Senate showdown appears headed to a run off next month if neither incumbent Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock nor Republican Herschel Walker can reach the 50 percent threshold. SEN. RAPHAEL WARNOCK (D-GA), SENATE CANDIDATE: You all just hang in there. I`m feeling good. HERSCHEL WALKER (R-GA), SENATE CANDIDATE: I told you he`s going to be tough to beat. You got to roll in Georgia here on. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Democrats showed signs of strength in a number of key races. GRAHAM: So you know, you got hats off to the Democrats. They perform well in a lot of these swing districts. ALEXANDER (voice-over): Two Democratic senators who`d been considered vulnerable New Hampshire`s Maggie Hassan and Colorado`s Michael Bennet, both fending off challenges overnight and in some of the country`s most competitive House races Democrats touting narrow victories including in Virginia. [07:05:04] REP. ABIGAIL SPANBERGER (D-VA): Thanks to your commitment and hard work we have won this race. ALEXANDER (voice-over): But some critical wins for the GOP holding on to a key Senate seat in North Carolina. And in Ohio, Republican political novice author J.D. Vance beating Democrat Tim Ryan . Vance was endorsed by former President Trump. J.D. VANCE (R-PA), SENATOR-ELECT: I will never forget where I came from, and I will never forget the great people of Ohio. ALEXANDER (voice-over): A major bright spot for the GOP Florida, Governor Ron DeSantis and Senator Marco Rubio cruising to reelection. Across the country, voters send a message that they`re dissatisfied with President Biden and particularly worried about the economy, with nearly a third saying in exit polls that rising inflation mattered most to them this year, but abortion rights was the second most important issue and a huge motivating factor for Democrats, now both parties facing a deeply divided electorate ahead of the next presidential election. (END VIDEOTAPE) ALEXANDER: And here in Pennsylvania, according to the NBC News exit poll, voters were confident in John Fetterman`s ability to serve this state effectively despite his health challenges. Dr. Mehmet Oz fell short of convincing those same Pennsylvanians that he had lived in this state long enough to serve it. Savannah and Hoda? GUTHRIE: All right, Peter Alexander leading us off. Thank you. KOTB: All right, let`s focus on that closely watched Senate battle in Georgia. It remains too close to call it this hour. NBC`s Gabe Gutierrez spent the night in Atlanta. His watching those results still coming in, have we seen any movement overnight, Gabe? GABE GUTIERREZ, NBC NEWS NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Hoda, good morning. Well, it was a long night here in Georgia. And we`re still at it, no clear winner. And NBC News has not projected this race but a runoff is appearing more and more likely at least that`s according to the Georgia Secretary of State`s office. Now incumbent senator Raphael Warnock is holding that slight lead over his challenger, football legend Herschel Walker . But there`s a third party candidate in this race. And according to Georgia State law, if no candidate reaches that 50 percent threshold, we`ll see a runoff here next month. Now this has been a wild race with more than a quarter billion dollars flowing into the state. And now voters in Georgia are preparing for the possibility of another four weeks of campaigning. Voters I`ve spoken with weren`t too thrilled about that. But in a second race, there was a clear victory. NBC News projects Republican Governor Brian Kemp defeating his Democratic challenger Stacey Abrams for the second time. And the vote tally so far is signaling that at least some Republicans may have voted for Kemp but then voted for the Democrat, Warnock. But again, this Senate race is still too close to call here. And depending on how a few other races go across the country. If we do head to a run off, it could be another several weeks before we know the balance of power in the Senate. Hoda? KOTB: All right, Gabe Gutierrez for us there in Atlanta. Gabe, thank you. GUTHRIE: Let`s go to another pivotal battleground, Arizona, the ballots in that state`s Senate and governor`s race still being counted. NBC`s Vaughn Hillyard is up early in Phoenix. Mark Kelly, the Senate incumbent holds the lead there, but we`re expecting these race results to tighten up. VAUGHN HILLYARD, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Yes, that`s right, Savannah. There are still hundreds of thousands of ballots to be counted here in this race. And it`s going to be challenger Blake Masters who is trying to take down incumbent Democratic Senator Mark Kelly. And you see that he`s down by about six percentage points right now though, but it`s important to note there is as much as one-third of the vote that is still outstanding, and much of that vote is expected to skew toward the GOP. Now election workers are returning here this morning in the Phoenix area to begin signature verifying these mail ballots that were received in recent days. This is going to be a slow process. We should also note the governor`s race, Kari Lake the Republican who is taking on Democratic Katie Hobbs , she well outpacing Masters. She is also losing at this hour to the Democrat. However, overnight, we saw the gap here shrink, and that is what the Republicans are hoping continuous here by weeks and that they are ultimately able to eclipse their Democratic opponent. Savannah? GUTHRIE: All right, Vaughn Hilliard in Arizona. Thank you. KOTB: As we mentioned earlier, we`re still waiting for results out of Nevada`s Senate race too. NBC`s Jacob Soboroff standing by in Vegas, Jacob this race was considered one of the most vulnerable for Democrats. So where do things stand this morning? JACOB SOBOROFF, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: It is still on the line, Hoda. Good morning to you. And Savannah to borrow a line from you last night, what happened in Vegas is going to stay in Vegas, at least for now. It`s not going to Washington, D.C. just quite yet. It was a nail biter out here. That`s what they expected and that is exactly what Senator Catherine Cortez Masto and her Republican challenger, the former state attorney general, Adam Laxalt got. They thought it was going to be a close race. That race is maybe even closer than they thought. Senator Cortes Masto acknowledged as much in a speech to supporters last night. We were there when she told those supporters that this race that hinged on the issues of abortion and the economy is now going to hinge on the pace with which with -- with which, excuse me, those ballots are ultimately going to be counted. And that is because state law here dictates a slow pace of count to ensure a fair and accurate election. [07:10:19] Now the question will be what is Adam Laxalt do? You`ll remember after the 2020 election here, he came out on behalf of President Trump and preemptively challenged the results of the election with baseless conspiracy theory election claims, saying that the election was stolen. That of course was debunked, proven as false by the Republican secretary of state here. Now that he`s in the lead. He took the lead overnight last night. Will he do the same thing? I guess we`ll have to find out today. Meanwhile, the vote count continues out here, guys. KOTB: All right, Jacob Soboroff in Vegas, Jacob, thank you. GUTHRIE: Well, let`s get to our national political correspondent, Steve Kornacki who`s been working the big board throughout the night. He`s back at it this morning. OK. I don`t think 24 hours ago we would have predicted that we wouldn`t know what is going to happen in the House yet. STEVE KORNACKI, NBC NEWS NATIONAL POLITICAL CORRESPONDENT: It`s amazing when you consider Republicans only needed a net gain of five seats to get control of the House. That was the closest a minority party was to winning the House coming into a midterm in nearly a century. And yet this morning, as you say, this is what our NBC News house model is showing. Our projection 218 is what you need to get a majority in the House. Our projection right now is that the Republicans will land at 220 critically plus or minus 10 seats. So in other words, there is very much a universe right now where Republicans could move north of 220 and end up with a majority somewhere around 10 seats or so. There is also a universe where the Democrats could retain control of the House. It remains undecided at this hour. GUTHRIE: And same goes for the Senate. Can we do the same thing on the Senate side? What`s the path to control there for both parties? KORNACKI: Yes, so let`s take a look at it. You heard some reports in the key states there. The big call over night was that Democrats picked up Pennsylvania. That means the Republicans need to gain two Democratic seats if they`re going to get control of the Senate. You see in yellow, what`s uncalled here. Ron Johnson is leading in Wisconsin. Let`s say Ron Johnson holds on to that Republicans would hold that seat. You got the report from Georgia where a runoff is a distinct possibility. Let`s say they do go to a runoff in Georgia, what that would mean is that between Arizona and Nevada, where you just heard those two reports, Republicans would for a moment need to win one of those two, their candidate is trailing in Arizona, their candidate has a lead in Nevada. So between those two, I think the Republicans if they`re going to win one, their prospects are probably better in Nevada than in Arizona. So let`s say the Democrats were to get Arizona, the Republicans were to get Nevada under a scenario like that. This Georgia, the runoff would end up being what decides control of the Senate. That runoff would be held on December 6th. And if the Democrats instead were to sweep Nevada in Arizona, that be it. They control the Senate. GUTHRIE: Well, can we go back to the House for a minute, let`s drill down on what exactly happened and where the Democrats are vulnerable at this hour. We saw what happened in Florida, it was basically a red sweep in Florida. It makes a huge difference for the Republicans. But there`s another place where Democrats are very vulnerable. KORNACKI: This is the surprise. All right, so Democrats have done vastly better than they imagined anyone imagined they would do. And yet look at New York State, right, one of the big blue states. What happened in New York State is the governor`s race, Kathy Hochul , the Democrat gets reelected, but it`s a close race and the Republican Lee Zeldin ran up huge numbers on Long Island and huge numbers upstate. And what that`s done is there`s just a whole bunch of House races in New York State in areas where Zeldin did well, where the Republicans are leading. Look at this one, Sean Patrick Maloney is the chairman of the DCCC, the committee that organizes the Democrats campaign strategy nationally. He is trailing in his own district. Democrats are trailing in two seats on Long Island. Democrats could lose five House seats out of New York. So we`re going through all that math right now, ironically enough, the biggest batch of outstanding results this morning is in New York. And there`s the prospect that Democrats could lose five of them there. That could end up being the difference in the House, New York. GUTHRIE: That`s fascinating to see how this is developing. Steve, thank you very much. Great job. KOTB: Let`s bring in NBC`s senior Washington correspondent Hallie Jackson had a very long night tracking results too. HALLIE JACKSON, NBC NEWS SENIOR WASHINGTON CORRESPONDENT: Are you ready for another month of this? KOTB: Well, sounds like it. Let`s talk about what was expected overnight. The polls expected that people were going to vote on inflation and crime that there was going to be a red wave. Yet, a lot of folks probably waking up at this hour going what happened to that red wave? So what did happened? JACKSON: Well, people did vote on inflation and abortion access and crime but it didn`t turn out the way that a lot of people had predicted or thought that it might turn out. As Steve is everybody has laid out here, no, we did not see that red wave materialize. And here`s why that matters, right, let`s say what happens in New York happens as Steve Kornacki has laid out and Republicans do take control of the House of Representatives. The margin matters, right, so whether they got 20 seats, 25 seats, which would be a wave versus like seven matters for a potential future House Speaker, Kevin McCarthy and how governing actually works, whether and how he`s able to wrangle the more far right elements of his caucus to create the laws that affect all of us. [07:15:27] GUTHRIE: Let`s talk about the Trump factor because many analysts are saying it played a role here in terms of the candidates that ran in some states, Trump-backed candidates were chosen in the primary did not perform well last night. Former President Trump out in force in a battleground like Pennsylvania, did that have an effect. JACKSON: Right, before Election Day too. Out in a bunch of battleground states in the four to five days before Election Day, I talked to several Democrats overnight in the wee hours of the morning, this morning, who suggests, yes, the Trump factor is because, why did you -- there all sites, right, I mean, I`ve talked to one PA, Democratic member of Congress, who is surprised happy but surprise. And I said, well, why, like what drove this? And I`ve had Democrats say to me, they do think part of it is the Trump factor here. The fact that when Donald Trump is in the news, Democrats are generally more motivated to come out and vote because it is obviously an anti-Trump vote, it`s not just that he was out in these battleground states like Pennsylvania, it`s that he`s also hinting he may be around for the next couple of years teasing a potential presidential run less than a week from today. KOTB: And just finally, how does the Biden administration feel about what happened overnight? JACKSON: Oh, I think they`re feeling pretty good at this moment. I think because, again, it is not what we expected. Democrats are looking surprisingly strong here today. The question is what does governing look like? I keep coming back to this because that`s what`s going to matter, right? When you look at economy, when you look at inflation, when you look at the potential things that a House, if it is in Republican control can do where does the Senate go? That`s going to be a big impact on how the White House can push anything through as far as a President Biden`s legislative agenda for the next two years. GUTHRIE: All right, Hallie, thank you so much. Catch a nap. There`s much more to talk about. Welcome in Craig, good morning to you. CRAIG MELVIN, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Hey, ladies. Good morning to both of you. To your point there, and good morning to you as well, with results still up in the air, it`s a waiting game in the White House to see what the future holds for President Biden`s agenda. NBC`s chief White House correspondent Kristen Welker joins us now, with more on that part of the story this morning, Kristen, what has been the reaction there so far? KRISTEN WELKER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Craig. Well, good morning. This morning, the president and the White House feeling pretty emboldened this morning after that Republican wave that we`ve been talking about that they feared seemingly never materialized. Now President Biden making calls to winners overnight advisors say, look, while inflation was still clearly a drag on the party, they were especially encouraged that the issue of abortion was a motivating factor for voters. Still you have some Democrats who are worried about their position looking forward to 2024. One of the President`s top allies, in fact, House Majority Whip Jim Clyburn saying overnight Democrats and I`ll read this, Craig, quote, may have to plan for 2024 differently. Does that mean bringing in new people? I don`t know. That`s a quote from Clyburn. But it raises questions about the President`s own future. Now a top Biden adviser telling me this morning nothing has changed about the President`s thinking he has consistently said he intends to run, hasn`t made that final decision yet. We will likely hear more from him about all of this a little bit later on today. Craig? MELVIN: I`m curious quote from Clyburn indeed though. Our chief White House correspondent Kristen Welker for us there, Kristen, thank you. Ladies? GUTHRIE: All right, yes, Craig, we have a lot more results and reaction for you a little bit later. You can find the very latest updates throughout the day on NBC News Daily and of course, tonight on NBC Nightly News. KOTB: And we also are following another major story this morning, a tropical storm, Nicole, bearing down on Florida. Mandatory evacuations have been ordered for parts of its east coast. Dylan is at her post. She`s in for Al once again. Hey, Dylan. DYLAN DREYER, NBC NEWS METEOROLOGIST: Good morning, guys. Yes, let`s start with tropical storm, a potential hurricane into the whole mix here. And we do have still a tropical storm at this time, but it`s very close to being a weak category one hurricane winds. All right, 70 miles per hour right now, it`s moving southwest fairly quickly at 13 mph is going to move through the Bahamas and likely strengthen to a category one hurricane before making landfall tonight into early tomorrow morning just north of West Palm Beach, Florida. Then it tracks across the peninsula here and then takes a turn up towards Tallahassee and then as it rains itself out, it`s going to bring a lot of rain into especially the interior northeast, as the tropical system does. It`s got a lot of water with it. So our biggest concern right now will be for some flash flooding. Also some storm surge flooding right along the east coast of Florida, parts of Florida, north of West Palm Beach, we can see about six to eight inches of rainfall. And then if we extend this up to where the storm is going through the weekend, interior parts of the Northeast could end up with about two to four inches of rain, so a flooding potential even in the Northeast going into the weekend. [07:19:52] That`s a look at the weather across the country. We`ll get to your local forecast in the next 30 seconds. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) (LOCAL NEWS) DREYER: And that`s your latest forecast. KOTB: All right. Thank you, Dylan. We`re also going to check in with Kerry Sanders. He`s alive on Daytona Beach just ahead. GUTHRIE: Plus, we`re going to break down that big night for Florida`s Governor Ron DeSantis , coasting to reelection and perhaps setting the stage for 2024. KOTB: And it`s the $2 billion question in the morning, who bought it? Who bought that winning Powerball ticket? We`ll take you live to a California gas station where it was sold. But first, this is Today on NBC. Oh, my God. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) GUTHRIE: Coming up, I can`t believe I missed this, the new season of "The Crown" made its debut overnight. Keir Simmons catching up with the casts. MELVIN: Yes, well, they want you to know about their take on life inside the royal family after your local news. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:26:21] (LOCAL NEWS) (COMMERCIAL BREAK) (LOCAL NEWS) (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:30:19] KOTB: We`re back now. It is 7:30. It`s a Wednesday morning. It`s November 9th, 2020. All glory outside. MELVIN: Can I just say, I went to sleep with you last night at like 12:00, 12:30. And now this morning -- GUTHRIE: We`re waking up together too. MELVIN: Fresh as a daisy. KOTB: But she only has one, two, three and I`m donating of course here. GUTHRIE: I know. One of these is jet fuel. KOTB: Yes, exactly. MELVIN: Well done. Well done last night. GUTHRIE: Yes, no pints. Not yet. That`s not until 8:40. Let`s get your headlines at 7:30 Wednesday morning. American basketball star Brittney Griner has been moved from a detention center to a Russian penal colony. Last month the Russian court rejected her appeal of that nine year sentence for drug possession. Her legal team says they do not know her exact current location. Russian penal colonies are notorious for overcrowding and harsh conditions. Inmates often subjected to manual labor. KOTB: Breaking overnight, North Korea fired at least one ballistic missile toward its eastern sea this morning, adding to a recent barrage of weapons tests. North Korea fired dozens of missiles last week in reaction to joint military exercises between the United States and South Korea. The North has launched more than 60 ballistic missiles so far this year. MELVIN: A Tyrannosaurus Rex skull unearthed in South Dakota could sell for as much as $20 million at auction next month. The 200 pound fossil nicknamed Maximus is being sold by an owner who wishes to remain anonymous. That skull by the way, it`s about 76 million years old. Experts say despite its age, it`s in remarkable condition. It has most of the external bones and numerous teeth as well. GUTHRIE: It doesn`t look a day over 75 million. MELVIN: SG, what you do with that if you buy it for 20 million? GUTHRIE: I don`t know. KOTB: Let`s turn back to more midterm results and reaction. MELVIN: Yes, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis cruise to victory winning reelection in a landslide over Democrat Charlie Crist . GUTHRIE: His performance cementing his status as a leading figure in the Republican Party boosting his stock as a 2024 presidential contender as well. NBC`s Ali Vitali is in Tampa this morning. She got that part of the midterm story. Hi, Ali, good morning. ALI VITALI, NBC NEWS CAPITOL HILL CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Savannah, good morning. You know, we all know the old Tim Russert mantra. It`s Florida, Florida, Florida. But even on a night like last night where Republicans won by sweeping margins, this state is still in the spotlight seen as more solidly red now than it`s been in years and boosting a new man to the front of the Republican pack. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) VITALI (voice-over): Overnight, a major midterm victory, possibly setting up a preview for the next presidential election. In Florida, Republican Governor Ron DeSantis cruising to reelection in a landslide over Charlie Crist . DESANTIS: I am honored by your support and I look forward to the road ahead. VITALI (voice-over): He`d had a tougher run four years ago winning by less than 1 percent. But Florida is a different state now. He`s projected to flip the key Miami Dade County, the first Republican governor to do so in over a decade. He along with Senator Marco Rubio solidifying GOP control of the one swing state. But DeSantis` victory also cemented his status as a Republican star and a possible front runner for the next presidential election. At his victory rally, the crowd chanting, two more years, signaling support for 2024 run. The Florida governor has made a name for himself in GOP circles over the last few years with his aggressive plans to reopen the state after the COVID pandemic and his fundraising prowess and he`s positioned himself as a key champion of the party, including in a recent ad. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: God looked down on his planned in paradise and said I need to protect her. VITALI (voice-over): All of it catching the attention of former President Donald Trump who has himself teased a 2024 run. Trump technically backing DeSantis but not sparing him, declaring himself the front runner over the weekend. DONALD TRUMP , FORMER PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: There it is Trump at 71 Ron DeSanctimonious at 10 percent. VITALI (voice-over): And previewing serious Republican infighting to come if both do run. GUTHRIE: Let me tell you what President Trump said today to an interview about Ron DeSantis . He said it would be a mistake if DeSantis won one and he said ran for president and he said if he did, Trump said he would say things about him that won`t be flattering, and said I know more about him than anybody. How does this sit with you? GRAHAM: Take it for what it`s worth. Here`s what I think. President Trump if he announces next week, which I think he`s likely to do, we`ll have about six months to himself. VITALI (voice-over): Graham adding that DeSantis has to be governor for a while before getting into the race. Republicans taking a wait and see approach as the popular governor may be gearing up to battle the party`s biggest star. (END VIDEOTAPE) [07:35:04] GUTHRIE: Oh, this could be war, Ali. We already see the rumblings. Are people that you`re talking to voters there who like DeSantis, like Trump? Are they conflicted, torn between these two potential candidates? VITALI: Yes, definitely, Savannah. Look, DeSantis is a popular governor. TRUMP is a popular former president. Voters that I`ve been talking to here over the last few weeks like both of them, many of them don`t want to have to make a choice but it looks like they`re both on a collision course. I really saw it last night as I was leaving the DeSantis event, a man came up to me wearing a Make America Great Again hat, unfurling a Trump 2024 banner. He said he hoped that Trump could run in 2024. And that DeSantis could wait until 2028. I don`t want to count that far ahead into the future. But it`s clear that voter`s minds are already there. And frankly, in my text with Republican donors, their minds are already there, too. They`re starting to make some early picks as the shadow primary becomes a lot more public now. GUTHRIE: All right, Ali, thank you so much. That`s the worst thing about the day after the midterms. They start talking about the next election. We can`t talk about 2028, no. KOTB: We need a minute here. GUTHRIE: Yes. KOTB: All right, guys, still ahead, the mystery and drama surrounding that record shattering Powerball jackpot. We are live at that gas station near L.A. where the winning ticket was sold, a single ticket after that hours long delay in the drawing. MELVIN: Hard to believe that. We`re also going to go back to Florida as well because millions in storm weary Florida are once again bracing for a possible hurricane in November. And it could strike as soon as tonight. We`re going to have a live report from Kerry Sanders and we`ll get Dylan`s forecast right after this. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:41:11] GUTHRIE: All right, we`re back. Let`s dig into it that record breaking Powerball drawing. There was the hours long mysterious delay and then somebody won. KOTB: That was totally weird. Well, it all came down to one single winning ticket it was sold. It was worth more than $2 billion. MELVIN: Yes. Dana Griffin clearly didn`t win because she is outside that store in Los Angeles, where the boarding ticket was purchased. Hey, Dana, good morning. DANA GRIFFIN, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Craig, good morning to you and everyone else. You know, after three months and a processing delay, we finally have a Powerball winner, the biggest in history. That $2 billion ticket was sold here at Joe Service Center in Altadena. The big question now, who has it? (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) GRIFFIN (voice-over): After 40 straight winless drawings, someone is taking home the largest lottery prize in history. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: This is Powerball. GRIFFIN (voice-over): This morning, one person is holding the only ticket matching all six winning Powerball numbers, the jackpot reaching $2,040,000,000 a lump sum payout will be more than 997 million before taxes. CAROLYN BECKER, CALIFORNIA LOTTERY SPOKESPERSON: Joe Service Center had the privilege of selling the only Powerball jackpot winning ticket. GRIFFIN (voice-over): That ticket sold just outside of Los Angeles at this gas station in Altadena, California. The jackpot so massive, lottery officials had to take the letter B on the winning billionaire banner. BECKER: We never had to do this. GRIFFIN (voice-over): The historic win came after a technical issue in Minnesota calls the drawing to experience a 10-hour delay. Now the lucky player is California lottery`s first ever billionaire. (on camera): The big question, who won? BECKER: It is the billion dollar question. The $2 billion question we don`t know who won. GRIFFIN (voice-over): No one has claimed the big prize yet, the winner won`t stay a mystery forever. California law requires their name to eventually be made public. Still, the advice from lottery experts lay low before claiming the record breaking payout. KURT PANOUSES, TAX ATTORNEY AND CPA: They need to take their time. They need to slow down. And as I always tell people, wait for the roller coaster to come to a stop before you try to get off. GRIFFIN (voice-over): But the newest billionaire won`t be the only one cashing in. More than 11 million tickets won something with cash prizes totaling $98 million including 3 more million dollar winners in the Golden State. The jackpot selling store`s owner Joseph Chahayed will also enjoy a million dollar bonus as we all wait for someone to claim that historic grand prize (on camera): What do you want to tell that person who is probably sitting at home trying to wrap his or her head? JOSEPH CHAHAYED, GAS STATION OWNER: I love you before and I love you know and I`m going to love you forever. (END VIDEOTAPE) GRIFFIN: So Papa Joe as he`s known around here is definitely filling that lottery love this morning. Now the winner has up to a year to claim that ticket. And if you weren`t the lucky winner, no worries. Guess what? There`s going to be another Powerball drawing tonight. Just a little smaller prize at $20 million, guys. MELVIN: All right, Dana Griffin, Dana, welcome to NBC News by the way. KOTB: Way to go, Dana. MELVIN: Welcome to the Peacock. KOTB: You did great report. GRIFFIN: Thank you. Thank you. Happy to be here. KOTB: All right. GUTHRIE: We won the lottery with her. MELVIN: There you go. Welcome to NBC. Let`s turn now to the latest on the new hurricane threat facing Florida this morning. KOTB: Yes, six weeks after and now Nicole taking aim at the state expected to gain strength before making landfall. We`re going to get to Dylan`s forecast in just a moment. But first, NBC`s Kerry Sanders he joins us from Daytona Beach shores. Hey, Kerry, good morning. KERRY SANDERS, NBC NEWS SENIOR NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT: Good morning guys. Look, you can see the Atlantic Ocean over my shoulder. It`s kicking up. The winds are picking up. The commercial airports in the area, that`s Orlando, Daytona Beach, Melbourne, they`re either closed or will be closing because of the approaching Tropical Storm that may become a Hurricane Nicole. [07:45:02] The big threat of course here is along the coast coastal erosion. And as you take a look at some of these pictures just leading into the arrival of Nicole, you`ll get a better understanding as to why Ian hammered this area and a lot of the coast was lost to the storm at the same time with the winds coming in. We have the threat to Artemis. OK. That rocket right now is sitting on the pad. It was supposed to launch on the 14th it`s now been pushed back to the 16th. It`s designed to withstand winds of about 85 miles per hour. But the real threat is going to be the rain. So NASA has put out staff to triple check all the hatches to make sure that everything is sealed. Meantime, mandatory evacuations from Flagler County all the way down to Martin County. Those who live in coastal Zone A have been told to leave. And as you saw from those pictures, the biggest threat of course with the coastal erosion is some of the buildings it`s feared by officials could actually have their foundations undermined and they could collapse. So a lot of attention anybody in a mobile home told also to go inland to shelters and then ultimately, tourists in the area who might be caught off guard, they should also find out where those shelters are. They`re open to everybody not just residents, guys. KOTB: Yes, good advice. Kerry Sanders for us there. Kerry, thank you. GUTHRIE: OK, let`s go to Dylan. She`s got the very latest on Nicole, the rest of today`s forecast in for Al this morning, hey. DREYER: Good morning again, guys. And I want to point out that hurricanes hitting the United States in November is pretty rare. We`ve only ever had it happen three times. So this would be the fourth one if this does strengthen into a category one storm. It is still a tropical storm, but it`s very close to being a weak category one so that`s why we do have your hurricane warnings in effect and it`s just north of West Palm Beach where we`re expecting landfall tonight, into tomorrow morning around 10:00 p.m. to about 2:00 a.m. tomorrow morning. And as this makes its way on shore, we are going to see that push of water. The good thing is it`s low tide when the storm is expected to make landfall but still on the backside of that your next high tide about six hours later, we could end up with a three to five foot storm surge. And we`re also looking for that to make its way up into the Northeast. Rainfall totals about eight inches possible in parts of Florida in the Northeast. We can see about two to four inches of rain. That`s a look at the weather across the country. Now here`s a peek out your window. (LOCAL NEWS) DREYER: And that`s your latest forecast. [07:48:03] KOTB: All right, Dylan, thank you. Still ahead, our exclusive look at a new and emotional interview with Jennifer Aniston she`s opening up about the public scrutiny that surrounds her private life and her secret struggles with fertility. CARSON DALY, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Good morning everybody. Good to see you. Coming up on PopStart. Jen on Jen, we got the very sweet message that J.Lo was sharing about her husband`s former wife. headline: What We Learned From Voters In This Week`s Elections About The Issues That Really Matter To Them And Where The Country May Be Headed From Here
story_text: [08:15:00] WILLIE GEIST: On election day, all of the polls, the punditry, the focus groups, and the tea leaves give way to voters. Energized by a swirl of issues, inflation, abortion, crime, immigration, and the very foundations of democracy, Americans turned out in near record midterm numbers to make a loud statement about what they`re seeing in the country and what needs to change. NBC News Capitol Hill Correspondent Ali Vitali looks closer in our "Sunday Focus". (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) ALI VITALI, NBC NEWS CAPITOL HILL CORRESPONDENT (voiceover): They were the midterms that few saw coming. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: What happened to the red wave, Congresswoman? VITALI (voiceover): History defying results. BIDEN: We lost fewer seats and House representatives in any democratic president`s first elected midterm, at least 40 years. VITALI (voiceover): Near record turnout and a twist in where the competitive seats really were. Dems holding on in red states like Kansas. While losing key seats in blue New York. REP. SEAN PATRICK MALONEY (D-NY): I don`t like to lose, but my opponent won this race. And he won it fair and square. VITALI (voiceover): The economy and inflation, the top issue for voters, and a weak point for Democrats who struggled to offer a clear response. But issues like abortion and threats to democracy acted as a dam to the previously predicted red wave for Republicans. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: I`m out to say where democracy. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: I don`t think that a body of strangers should tell us what our choices should be. VITALI (voiceover): In crucial states like Michigan and Pennsylvania, abortion rights surpassed inflation as voters` number one concern, allowing Democrats to notch key governor and Senate race wins and quiet gains on the state level. Dems not losing a single state legislative chamber for the first time in nearly 90 years. Back in Washington, Republicans now grappling with how it could have gone so wrong. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Look, I`m frustrated that it didn`t turn out well for us. VITALI (voiceover): From once predicting a more than 20-seat margin in the House of Representatives to just being happy with a majority. REP. KEVIN MCCARTHY (R-CA): What`s was our mission? To win the majority, to stop Biden`s agenda, and fire Nancy Pelosi . All of that is accomplished. VITALI (voiceover): Maybe, but if Republicans do take the House, it`ll be very slim margins. Giving all members more power. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: I think it`s wonderful because everybody`s voice needs to be considered. [08:20:00] VITALI (voiceover): And GOP Leader Kevin McCarthy. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Oh, I think there`s some questions about leadership. VITALI (voiceover): His future as house speaker now thrown into flux. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: I expect there will be a challenge. VITALI (voiceover): But amid a week of surprises, one important traditional hallmark, candidates who lost saying so. TIM MICHELS (R-WIS) GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE: Unfortunately, the math doesn`t add up. I just called Governor Evers and conceded. I wish the Evers family well. VITALI (voiceover): Not necessarily a given. With nearly 300 election deniers on the ballot and a former president insisting they make election denialism a central focus. KARI LAKE (R-AZ) GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE: Trump won, you`re right. VITALI (voiceover): That said, more than half of election denying candidates won their races, many coming to Congress now in 2023. And in the aftermath, Republicans also reckoning with the Trump of it all. Many of his hand-picked candidates lost. DONALD TRUMP , FORMER U.S. PRESIDENT: Well, I think if they win, I should get all the credit. And if they lose, I should not be blamed at all. VITALI (voiceover): While pro-democracy candidates won in key states. KELLY: No one party has a monopoly on good ideas. VITALI (voiceover): One of the Democrat`s strongest voting blocs, Gen Z. young voters showing up in record numbers. Rallying around things like student loan forgiveness. Among them, 25-year-old Maxwell Frost who won his election in Florida, making him the first Gen Zer elected to Congress. CROWD: Maxwell. Maxwell. VITALI (voiceover): And in a midterm election full of firsts, another. A record $17 billion spent on campaigns and ads. All for the country to wake up Wednesday pretty much how it went to bed on election night, divided down the middle. (END VIDEO CLIP) GEIST: And Ali joins me now live. Ali, good morning. It`s great to see you. So, after the stunning midterm elections, there`s been a lot of talk about Republicans walking away from Donald Trump , but we`ve heard that before. VITALI (on camera): Yes. GEIST: And the former president made it very clear again this week, he will not go quietly or perhaps at all. VITALI: Yes, that`s right, because Mr. Trump is expected to announce another run for president this week down at Mar-a-Lago. But it comes as the party that he`s controlled for the last six years has spent the last week actively pondering a future or as "The New York Post" said, a defuture without him. One of the names that keeps coming up for 2024 is Florida Governor Ron DeSantis . But we know that former V.P. Mike Pence , former Ambassador Nikki Haley, former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo , also others, they all likely have their eyes on the presidential prize this coming cycle. And while Mr. Trump`s had a bad political week, we have seen this time and again, Willie, Republicans end up going back and sticking by the former president. So, time will tell if this moment is actually any different. Willie. GEIST: Yes, see you January 6th for that. VITALI: Yes, exactly. GEIST: Meanwhile, we wake up this morning Democrats in control of the Senate. And as Steve Kornacki told us again last night, the house still very much in play. VITALI: Yes. GEIST: Extraordinary. Ali, thank you very much. Coming up next a new "Sunday Sitdown" with Daniel Radcliffe on the fun of playing "Weird Al" Yankovic in a new movie and the rocket ride of being "Harry Potter". And then a life well-lived, the pioneering journalist who broke down the locker room door for the women who came after her. And as we head to break, our photo of the week. The iconic Dolly Parton performing at last weekend`s Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony in Los Angeles. After initially saying she did not think belonged in that hall, Dolly finally relented to the fans and accepted the honor. She even wrote and performed a new song for the occasion called "Rockin`". Dolly joined in this year`s class by Duran Duran, Eminem, Lionel Richie, Carly Simon, among others. Congratulations to Dolly, our national treasure. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [08:25:00] (LOCAL NEWS) (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [08:30:00] (LOCAL NEWS) (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) CECILY STRONG, ACTRESS: The Maricopa County officials are incompetent. And it`s my belief that the election is rigged and the results should be thrown out. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: It sounds like new numbers coming in which has you taking a narrow lead over Katie Hobbs . STRONG: Which is why I have always said, this is democracy. Trust the system. Trust the voters. (END VIDEO CLIP) GEIST: That is Cecily Strong as Arizona Republican Gubernatorial candidate Kari Lake on last night`s new episode of "Saturday Night Live." headline: MTP for November 20, 2022, NBC
story_text: [09:00:00] (COMMERCIAL BREAK) CHUCK TODD, NBC HOST (voiceover): This Sunday, my interview with Former Vice President Mike Pence . MIKE PENCE, FORMER VICE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: For me, the fuse was lit in mid-November. TODD: His inside account of January 6th and how he broke with Donald Trump . PENCE: All I know is that what the president asked me to do, I would have violated my oath to the Constitution. TODD: What he thinks should happen now that Trump is running for office again. TODD (on camera): Do you think a crime was committed? PENCE: I don`t know if it is criminal to listen to bad advice from lawyers. TODD (voiceover): His thoughts on the midterms. PENCE: We had some surprising and disappointing results. TODD: And who he blames for Trump`s election denial. PENCE: I was disappointed in Mark Meadows ` performance as chief of staff. TODD: Plus his criticism of Attorney General Merrick Garland for approving the FBI search of Trump`s Florida home. PENCE: I have great concerns about his judgment in the leadership of the Justice Department. TODD: And his belief that the Supreme Court`s decision overturning Roe v. Wade was the single most important achievement of the Trump administration. PENCE: I celebrate that from really the depths of my heart. TODD: The former vice president opens up, as he considers his own run for the White House. Joining me for inside (inaudible), "New York Times" Chief White House Correspondent Peter Baker, Republican strategist Brendan Buck, Kimberly Atkins Stohr, senior opinion writer for "The Boston Globe ," and Anna Palmer, co-founder of Punchbowl News. TODD (on camera): Welcome to Sunday, it`s "Meet the Press." ANNOUNCER: From NBC News in Washington, the longest running show in television history, this is "Meet the Press" with Chuck Todd. (END VIDEO CLIP) TODD (on camera): Good Sunday morning. We are following the breaking news reports of a shooting overnight at a gay nightclub in Colorado Springs, Colorado. At least five people are dead, and another 18 so far are wounded. Police say the suspect was injured, is in custody, and is currently receiving treatment at a local hospital. The FBI is already on the scene and assisting local law enforcement. In a statement on their Facebook page, the club writes, "Club Q is devastated by the senseless attack on our community. We thank the quick reactions of heroic customers that subdued the gunman and ended this hate attack." Do stay tuned to NBC News for more updates on this shooting. You can get those at nbcnews.com as well. Turning now to politics, Republicans have taken back control of the House, squeaking into a narrow majority. But the biggest question after a disappointing midterm performance, the third disappointing election cycle in a row for the GOP, will Republicans rally behind Donald Trump yet again? Seven-hundred-and-twenty-one days before the next presidential election, Donald Trump became one of a small group of ex-presidents to announce he will again seek another term even after being defeated. Just one of those ex-presidents, Grover Cleveland, has been successful doing this. The timing of the announcement at his gated Palm Beach resort appears to be an effort to get ahead of several federal criminal investigations, and on Friday, in reaction, Attorney General Merrick Garland appointed a special counsel to take over investigations he was overseeing into the former president`s role in the events leading up to the January 6th attack on the Capitol, as well as the former president`s decision to retain classified government documents at Mar-a-Lago. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) MERRICK GARLAND , UNITED STATES ATTORNEY GENERAL: Based on recent developments, including the former president`s announcement that he is a candidate for president in the next election, and the sitting president`s stated intention to be a candidate as well, I have concluded that it is in the public interest to appoint a special counsel. (END VIDEO CLIP) TODD: The attorney general`s goal is to create some political distance between that investigation and obviously the Biden administration. That`s the reason for this appointment. Jack Smith is a longtime federal prosecutor, who has mostly -- most recently been working at the International Criminal Court at the Hague. Now if Trump falters in his presidential campaign, there are a handful of Republican hopefuls that are ready to challenge him, including his former vice president, Mike Pence . Pence`s new memoir, "So Help Me God" actually was out perhaps not so coincidently, the same day that his running mate, Donald Trump , announced. And he describes Trump`s pressure campaign in the book on him to refuse to certify the 2020 elections, which of course culminated when rioters threatened Mike Pence`s life. I spoke to the former vice president at the Reagan Presidential Library in Simi Valley, California. And I began by asking him about his likely run for president. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) TODD: The former president has said it`s disloyal for some of the Republican Party to challenge him, and he`s speaking about not just you but Governor DeSantis, Secretary Pompeo. Do you accept the idea that running against him is disloyal? [09:05:00] PENCE: I think the American people love competition. My loyalty is to my faith, to my values, and to America. And I think if we`re a part of that debate next year, and our family will sort that out before the end of the year, Chuck -- TODD: Right. PENCE: -- or if we`re just chipping in from the sidelines and others are in that contest, I think a good, healthy debate over the direction of the country is warranted. I mean, since the first days of the Biden/Harrison administration, it almost seems as though we have a new Democratic administration intent on weakening America at home and abroad. Whether it`s the disastrous withdrawal from Afghanistan, whether it be the gusher of spending that ignited the worst inflation in 40 years, the war on energy that`s caused gasoline price to go through the roof, our crime wave in our major cities, and of course, after undoing all the successful policies that secured our southern border, we now have the worst crisis at our southern border in American history. And so I truly do believe that Republican primary voters want to hear a strong debate, they`ll want to find our best standard bear (ph) so that having won back the House, which became official this last week, we`ll have a chance to win back America in 2024. TODD: You laid out a reason why you think the Biden administration has led America down a path that you don`t like. Why do you think voters didn`t accept that premise in 2022? They clearly didn`t in the battleground states. Why do you think that was? PENCE: Well, they did in many states around the country. It`s a -- in the state of New York, four new Republican congressmen elected, may well be the margin of the majority itself. And the state of Iowa, for the first time in a half a century, they`ll have all Republican members of the House of Representatives. But, Chuck, I take your point. A win is a win. I`m glad to see Kevin McCarthy will accept the gavel to be the next speaker of the House, but I`d like to see more Republicans elected. And I`d liked to seen Republicans win the Senate and more governorships around the country. But for me, the common denominator had to do with whether or not candidates were focused on the future. As I traveled around the country -- TODD: That sounds like that`s code for whether or not candidates were sort of in the Trump spell. PENCE: Well, I don`t -- TODD: I mean, I think you`re trying to be polite. I understand that. But it does seem that what you`re saying is anybody that was close to Trump didn`t do well. PENCE: But I think it`s broader than that, Chuck. For me, as I travel -- and I went to 35 states in the last year and a half, campaigning for all kinds of men and women, running for statewide office, and for the House and the Senate. And as I sort through the results, there really is a common denominator, candidates that were focused on the issues that people are facing today and solutions for tomorrow, focused on the future did quite well, but candidates that were focused on the past, candidates that were focused on relitigating the 2020 election did not fare as well. When -- and we had some surprising and disappointing results. TODD: You stopped short of saying that the former president is unfit to serve again. But as former defense secretary Mark Esper says he`s unfit for office, another former defense secretary Jim Mattis says Trump has no moral compass. Bill Barr, the attorney general, he has neither the temperament nor the persuasive powers. Judge Luttig, somebody you admire, I know, Trump and his apologists are a clear and present danger to American democracy. Is he fit to serve as president of the United States for another four years? PENCE: I really do believe that`s a decision for the American people. And President Trump is now -- TODD: Isn`t your opinion -- (CROSSTALK) TODD: -- you think your opinion matters to the American people?
