headline: The Today Show for February 20, 2023, NBC
story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [08:00:00] SHEINELLE JONES, NBC NEWS 3RD HOUR OF TODAY, CO-HOST: It is 8:00 on "TODAY." Coming up, surprise visit. Overnight, President Biden making history arriving in Ukraine. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) JOE BIDEN , U.S. PRESIDENT: I`m here to show our unwavering support for the nation`s independence, and sovereignty, and territorial integrity. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: A major sign of support from the U.S. as the war in Ukraine approaches its one-year anniversary. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) BIDEN: That`s how long we`re going to be with you, Mr. President, for as long as it takes. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: We`re live with the latest. Then, holiday sales. Hoping to save some money this long weekend. We have a look at all the best Presidents` Day deals, everything from furniture to appliances, electronics, and cars. Plus, the three questions you should ask yourself before making a purchase. And royal treatment. The Prince and Princess of Wales joining stars from around the world for the so-called British Oscars. We`re highlighting all the best moments including an emotional tribute to Queen Elizabeth. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) HELEN MIRREN, ACTRESS: Cinema at its best does what her majesty did effortlessly, bring us together and unite us in a story. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: So, what films took home the night`s biggest awards? All that and more. Today, Monday, February 20, 2023. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Spending Presidents` Day. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: On the plaza. CROWD: From Fort Worth, Texas. CROWD: Murrysville (ph), Pennsylvania. CROWD: Huntsville, Alabama. CROWD: St. John, Indiana. CROWD: And New Lenox, Illinois. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Celebrating milestone birthdays. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: My 30th. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: And my 60th. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: From Jacksonville, Florida. CROWD: Lea`s (ph) turning 18. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Shout out to our NBC family. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: At KOMU 8 News. CROWD: In Columbia, Missouri. CROWD: Happy Presidents` Day. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: Welcome back to "TODAY." We certainly appreciate you being with us on this Monday morning. And take a look at all of these folks. We are happy to see this happy holiday crowd. This is on -- in our corner of the woods here at Rockefeller Plaza. TOM LLAMAS, NBC NEWS SENIOR NATIONAL CORRESPONDENT: Yes, they came from all over the country. We always love that. JONES: Uh-huh. LLAMAS: A lot of states represented. Savannah and Hoda, you know them, will be back tomorrow, of course, and it will be a big morning here in Studio 1A. JONES: That is right. Grammy winning superstar Pink will be here. She`s coming out with a new album and heading on tour. So, a lot to talk about. Plus, she`ll treat us to a live performance when she joins us for our 8:00, 9:00, and 10:00 hours. So, join us tomorrow. JACOB SOBOROFF, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: I am not going anywhere. LLAMAS: Yes. JONES: Right SOBOROFF: I`m going to stick around for that. JONES: It`s going to be a party. LLAMAS: She always brings it. Like, live -- JONES: She does. LLAMAS: -- Pink live is always amazing. JONES: She does. And we`ll get back outside and say hi to all those folks coming up in just a bit. Meantime, it is a busy morning. So, let`s get to your news at 8:00. In an unprecedented show of support for Ukraine, President Biden took a high stakes trip to the war zone overnight. His surprise journey to Kyiv coming just days before the first anniversary of the Russian invasion. NBC`s Erin McLaughlin is in the Ukrainian capital with more on this historic visit. Erin, good morning. ERIN MCLAUGHLIN, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Good morning, Sheinelle. President Zelenskyy calling the visit historic, timely, and brave. The visit began here in the capital at the presidential palace. President Biden was greeted by President Zelenskyy and his wife, Olena. He signed a guest book and announced a $500 million military aid package and delivered this message. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) JOE BIDEN , U.S. PRESIDENT: One year later, Kyiv stands and Ukraine stands, democracy stands. America stands with you and the world stands with you. (END VIDEO CLIP) MCLAUGHLIN: From the palace, they made their way to St. Michael`s Cathedral. I watched as air raid sirens echoing in the distance. The two presidents walked out this way and paid tribute to the thousands of fallen Ukrainian soldiers in the memorial behind me. From there, President Biden made his way to the U.S. embassy where he met with staff before departing the capital. In Russia, this visit is being seen as a provocation. But here in Ukraine, it is being seen as a remarkable show of support and solidarity by America. Back to you. JONES: All right. Erin, thank you. LLAMAS: And as we just saw there, the president`s secret trip showing his unwavering support for Ukraine, even as some in NATO and in Congress are questioning the ongoing commitment. NBC`s Chief White House Correspondent and Weekend TODAY co-anchor Kristen Welker joins us now live from Poland where the president will be marking this week`s first anniversary of the war. Kristen, good morning. KRISTEN WELKER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT AND "SATURDAY TODAY" ANCHOR: Hi, Tom. Good morning to you. That`s right. [08:05:00] This trip was so secret because of the dangers that it posed, that only a handful of the president`s inner staff was aware that he was actually traveling to Kyiv. And that keen message just adding to what Erin said, the president saying, we`re not leaving. But executing on that is going to be more challenging to keep the global community on board and Congress, with some Republicans, already saying they are not going to write a blank check to Ukraine. So, what happens now? Well, he travels here to Poland. He`s going to be meeting with the president of Poland. He will be meeting with leaders of the critical eastern flank and then he`s going to deliver his capstone address in the same location where he spoke in Warsaw when he visited when the war was just a month old. And I am told in talking to top officials, that part of his message is going to be a condemnation of Vladimir Putin building on what we heard from the vice president over the weekend, that Putin has committed crimes against humanity and should be held accountable. Now, this all comes amid new concerns about China, it`s believed that China is providing nonlethal aid to Russia. The secretary of state, over the weekend, saying that they believe China is considering providing lethal aid as well. The secretary of state warning that would be met with serious consequences, all as this war enters a pivotal new phase. Tom. LLAMAS: All right. Kristen Welker with a lot of new developments there. Kristen, thank you. SOBOROFF: Breaking overnight, North Korea fired two short-range ballistic missiles towards Japan today, it`s second weapons test in the last three days. The missiles landing in the waters off the west coast of Japan. The test prompting Tokyo to call for an emergency meeting of the United Nations Security Council . Over the weekend North Korea also launched an intercontinental ballistic missile, and in response, the U.S. military yesterday held bilateral air drills with South Korea and Japan. JONES: All right. We`ve covered the news. Now, are you ready for a "Morning Boost"? LLAMAS: Yes. SOBOROFF: Yes, please. JONES: All right. This is a good one. A young Australian basketball fan was in tears after watching his team, the Tasmanian Jackjumpers get knocked out of the playoffs during a game in New Zealand. While on his way back to the locker room the Australian captain noticed the heartbroken fan and knew that he had traveled a long way to come see the game. So, he walked over to comfort him and even gave him a pair of sneakers. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED MALE: How is that, mate? UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Amazing. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Wow. CLINT STEINDL, TASMANIA JACKJUMPERS BASKETBALL TEAM CAPTAIN: As much as I try to put a smile on his face, he still had the tears. But maybe puts them up in his bedroom or something, gives him something to aspire to. And that`s what we`re trying to do in Tasian (ph), you know, I just try to help the little fella out. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: Oh, that`s sweet. A little classy move. Keeping in mind that the player has got to be hurting too from that season ending loss. Listen, there are fans young and old, and it hurts when you lose, you know. LLAMAS: Yes, that`s -- SOBOROFF: Shout out to the Jackjumpers. JONES: There you go. LLAMAS: Tasmanian Jackjumpers. I like those jerseys too. SOBOROFF: Nice. JONES: Learn something everything. LLAMAS: Those are pretty cool. All right. Coming up, the Prince and Princess of Wales rubbing elbows with the stars of Hollywood. We`re going to take you live to London for an inside look at the big night at the British version of the Oscars. JONES: But first, expert tips you need to hear to make the most of today`s holiday sales. We`ll get to that in a moment right after this. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [08:10:00] JONES: Welcome back this morning on "TODAY`s Consumer". We are focusing on those Presidents` Day sales. LLAMAS: Yes, inflation is putting a strain on your budget, it could be a great day to find a few deals, but, of course, there are things you need to consider. JONES: Joining us now is CNBC`s Senior Personal Finance Correspondent Sharon Epperson. Sharon, good morning to you. SHARON EPPERSON, CNBC`S SENIOR PERSONAL FINANCE CORRESPONDENT: Good morning. JONES: All right. Before we get into it, you say, before we get to the deals, you have three questions you want people to ask themselves. EPPERSON: Very important questions to ask. JONES: OK. EPPERSON: First of all, do you need it? JONES: Fair. EPPERSON: Do you love it? And can you pay it off immediately? JONES: Fair enough. EPPERSON: And so, it`s not just can you afford it. Because you`re probably going to put it on a credit card. JONES: Yes. EPPERSON: You don`t want to carry that interest on the credit card. You want to pay that off immediately or that savings is really something you`re going to be paying for, for months and months in interest. JONES: So, can you pay it within the month before you get that bill? EPPERSON: Exactly. JONES: All right. Fair enough. LLAMAS: I feel that`s a good life lesson -- JONES: It is. LLAMAS: -- not just for Presidents` Day. JONES: It is. I know. That is good. LLAMAS: Speaking of Presidents` Day, talk about some of the deals. EPPERSON: Well, there are a lot of different deals. A lot of people look at mattresses for Presidents` Day, furniture, maybe electronics. You may think about home appliances, large ones or little gadgets for your kitchen. LLAMAS: Uh-huh. EPPERSON: Maybe even a new car. So, there are a lot of different deals out there. I think I seem to be getting messages all the time about this deal or that deal for Presidents` Day doesn`t necessarily mean it`s something that I need. JONES: Right, right. EPPERSON: So, I kind of delete that message. LLAMAS: OK. All right. JONES: So, you were saying -- what about like kitchen or -- the kitchen appliances, are we talking like coffee pots or like refrigerators, like big ticket items? EPPERSON: There are some big ticket items too that are -- that you can get. One of the things to keep in mind when you`re talking about appliances, whether they`re large or small, as you`re often sold a or asked to purchase a warranty, an extended warranty -- JONES: OK. EPPERSON: -- or sometime service agreement. JONES: OK. EPPERSON: Important thing to check out there is to make sure that you actually really need that because it`s not going to be lasting that long. And that you could use that money, perhaps, to put into a savings account to buy a new one. What`s the replacement cost of that? JONES: That`s right. EPPERSON: Do you need to buy the extended warranty or the service agreement. JONES: The service agreement. LLAMAS: All right. Let`s dig a little deeper here. I know a family shopping around for a TV. Is it -- are electronics good right now? Is it a day to shop for electronics? EPPERSON: Well, there are large electronics. Some people want TVs, some people want a laptop or maybe something else for their, you know, sound system or something like that. Again, the important thing to think about is, one, not carrying the credit card debt if you`re going to put it on the card. But also, think about how much that energy is costing on your home. I`m thinking about everything I have on in my house right now when I`m not there. Why do I have my TV on -- LLAMAS: Right. EPPERSON: -- or my laptop on -- JONES: The energy vampire. EPPERSON: The energy vampires. The energy vampires can cost $250 a year in your house if they`re sucking energy -- LLAMAS: Oh. EPPERSON: -- because you don`t use it. So, think about that. As you`re thinking about what to purchase, keep in mind that maybe you don`t need that extra TV or if you get it, don`t have it on all the time. JONES: That`s fair. LLAMAS: OK. That`s good to know. JONES: But if you`re looking for a car, is now the time? A new car. EPPERSON: Well, there are going to be deals out there for new cars. Inventory is not tremendous, so there are going to be special deals for certain models. But again, the thing to think about is how are you going to pay for this car? And shopping around to get the best loan is very important. You`re going to see perhaps six percent or more for a five-year car loan on average. You could go to a credit union and get far less than maybe you pay through the dealer in terms of the loan or even a bank. So, make sure you shop around for a car loan and look at credit unions for a good place to get that loan. LLAMAS: Real quick on that before we go, should you call first or just go on the website? What`s the best when you`re dealing with credit unions or the banks? EPPERSON: Well, I think it`s great to go on websites to kind of consolidate all of the different -- give you all the options -- LLAMAS: Yes. EPPERSON: -- to look at. And then I absolutely think you should be calling or contacting the financial institution directly. LLAMAS: All right. JONES: That`s good advice. Thank you, Sharon. LLAMAS: Yes. EPPERSON: Absolutely. JONES: Happy, I guess, shopping. I didn`t -- expect to say, I guess -- LLAMAS: Presidents` Day. JONES: Yes, Presidents` Day shopping. But you have to be smart about it. EPPERSON: Smart. Smart shopping. JONES: Exactly. For more on the holiday sales, be sure to check out today.com/shop. Now, let`s head over to Dylan for the weather. DYLAN DREYER, NBC NEWS 3RD HOUR OF TODAY CO-HOST AND METEOROLOGIST: Good morning again, everyone. We do have some pretty decent weather for today, especially across the southeast where temperatures will be well above average. We do have a little bit of light rain falling through Kentucky and into Tennessee. And little light snow about to move through Central Minnesota through Minneapolis and Saint Paul, Billings. Also seeing some of that light snow too. [08:15:00] Now, there`s a bigger storm system that`s going to make its way across the country. It`s just bringing rain to the coast of Washington State right now but that will eventually turn into a big snow maker for the Rockies, also, across the Upper Midwest by the middle of the week. So, enjoy what`s out there right now. 50s and 60s up into the Carolinas, that`s above average for this time of year. 80s down through Texas. 80s into Florida too. And we are looking for temperatures to get well up into the 90s which could break all-time record high temperatures for the month of February in Florida, especially Wednesday and Thursday. So, this cold front is going to cool things off a little bit for the northeast. Again, we`ll watch that snow system -- the stormy system begins to move eastward as we go through the middle of the week. And it also looks nice in the southwest, a bit breezy, temperatures though with that sunshine in the 60s and 70s. That`s a look at the weather across the country. Now, here`s a peek out your window. (LOCAL NEWS) DREYER: And that is your latest forecast. JONES: All right. Thank you, Dylan. Now, Jacob, you`re covering "POP Start" for Carson today? SOBOROFF: Sure am. Ladies and gentlemen, here is your "POP Start." First up, "Back to the Future". JONES: What? LLAMAS: What? SOBOROFF: Believe it or not, it`s been almost four decades since Doc Brown gave us this lesson in time travel. Watch. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) CHRISTOPHER LLOYD, ACTOR, "BACK TO THE FUTURE": According to the flier at precisely 10:04 p.m. this Saturday night lightening will strike the clocktower, electrifying the cable just as a connecting hook makes contact thereby sending 1.21 gigawatts into the flux capacitor and sending you back to 1985. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: I love it. SOBOROFF: 1.21 gigawatts. JONES: Yes. SOBOROFF: Fast forward to the future, and the cast, you`re not going to believe this, is back together. JONES: Awe. DREYER: Oh, that`s nice. SOBOROFF: How cool is this? Over the weekend, you see Christopher Lloyd, Michael J. Fox, Lea Thompson, Tom Wilson. Everybody reunited for a fan expo in Portland, Oregon. LLAMAS: Oh, OK. SOBOROFF: And the iconic former castmates shared a few sweet snaps -- JONES: That`s awesome -- SOBOROFF: -- from behind the scenes. Michael J. Fox said of this whole thing, some of my favorite people. JONES: I love that. SOBOROFF: One of the best. DREYER: I love it. SOBOROFF: One of the best. LLAMAS: One of the best. SOBOROFF: One of the best. LLAMAS: Yes. SOBOROFF: Yes, I miss the ride at Universal Studios. Bring it back, guys, bring it back. Next up, Rebel Wilson. Exciting announcement from the "Pitch Perfect" star. She is engaged. On Sunday, Wilson shared the happy news on social media posting this picture alongside fiance Ramona Agruma. The pair surrounded by flower petals during the proposal and Rebel also revealing a close-up of Ramona`s very sparkling Tiffany ring, captioning that post, we said, yes. Huge congratulations to those guys. Really, really awesome guys JONES: Absolutely. SOBOROFF: And coming up next, the BAFTA. Basically, it`s British -- the British version of the Oscars, one of the most prestigious awards in film. And last night, stars from around the world were out, including the Prince and Princess of Wales. Molly Hunter has that story. Hello "POP Start" correspondent. Good to see you. MOLLY HUNTER, NBC NEWS FOREIGN CORRESPONDENT: Hey, Jacob. Yes, it was a star-studded event. The BAFTAs are always super fun. But really, the highlight, one of the real winners of last night was one of the queens of Hollywood offering her tribute, a very special tribute to the late Queen Elizabeth. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) HUNTER (voiceover): Last night`s BAFTA awards weren`t just packed full of A-listers, but for the first time in two years, royalty was back. The Prince and Princess of Wales stepping out on the red carpet, Prince William, the president of the British Academy of film and Television Arts sporting a black velvet tuxedo. White Kate promoting sustainability, restyling an Alexander McQueen gown she first wore to the BAFTAs in 2019. It`s Britain`s most glamorous night and the highlight was a special tribute to the late Queen Elizabeth led by Dame Helen Mirren. HELEN MIRREN, ACTRESS: Cinema at its best does what her majesty did effortlessly, bring us together and unite us in a story. MCLAUGHLIN (voiceover): The queen honored with a BAFTA in 2013 for her long-standing patronage of the arts. MIRREN: Your majesty, you were our nation`s leading star. MCLAUGHLIN (voiceover): The tribute bringing a rare public show of emotion from Prince William. Mirren, who won both a BAFTA and an Oscar for her portrayal of the queen, shared what the tribute meant to her. MIRREN: You know, I`m Elizabethan, you know. She was there for my whole life. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Yes. MIRREN: And so, her passing was, you know -- UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: It was massive, wasn`t it? MIRREN: It was massive. MCLAUGHLIN (voiceover): As for the awards a teaser for the possible Oscar favorites. Kerry Condon and Barry Keoghan of "Banshees of Inisherin" both took supporting actor categories. BARRY KEOGHAN, ACTOR, "BANSHEES OF INISHERIN": For the kids that are dreaming to be something from the area that I came from, this is for you. HUNTER (voiceover): Austin Butler continued his winning streak adding to his Golden Globe win by taking home best leading actor for "Elvis". AUSTIN BUTLER, ACTOR, "ELVIS": This is amazing. [08:20:00] UNIDENTIFIED MALE: And the BAFTA goes to Cate Blanchett for "Tar". HUNTER (voiceover): Cate Blanchett added a BAFTA best actress to her resume for her performance in "Tar". Catherine Zeta Jones, Actress: "All Quiet on the Western Front". HUNTER (voiceover): And in dominating fashion, the German anti-war movie "All Quiet on the Western Front" led the way with seven BAFTAs, including best director and best film. (END VIDEO CLIP) HUNTER (on camera): Now, what an exciting night. Now, we are also getting closer and closer, of course, to the next major event on the royal calendar, the coronation in May, of course. The palace has released the coronation emblem, you guys. I think we have a picture, actually, to show you. It represents the flora of the four nations. It honors King Charles`s love of the natural world. Now, we are also learning about the music that will be played at the coronation, including a brand-new composition by, of course, famed composer, Andrew Lloyd Webber . Guys, I`ll send it back to you. LLAMAS: Oh, OK. JONES: Very cool. LLAMAS: Yes. DREYER: Nice. JONES: All right. Molly Hunter, thank you so much. And guys, finally, it is Monday. You know what that means. A new episode of Hoda`s hit podcast "Making Space" just came out, just seconds ago. You can find it by scanning the QR code on the bottom of your screen. Today`s episode a season three finale, unfortunately. It features guest Rosie Perez -- JONES: Oh, fun. SOBOROFF: -- not unfortunately, during their inspirational conversation, the Oscar nominated actress shared her candid thoughts on aging. Listen. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS TODAY, CO-ANCHOR: I feel like the best is now. Do you feel that? ROSIE PEREZ, ACTRESS: Me too, it is. And you know, someone said, oh, my God. You`re almost -- going to be 60. KOTB: Yes. PEREZ: I go, I can`t wait. KOTB: Yes. PEREZ: Because if this is -- if this is getting good now, oh, my God. You know what I mean? I was like I cannot wait. I really cannot wait. And I -- you know, I told my husband, I said, every single day I`m getting out of my own way. KOTB: Uh-huh. PEREZ: Every single day and it`s getting a little bit better. Every single day. (END VIDEO CLIP) SOBOROFF: All right. Guys, you can listen to their full conversation -- LLAMAS: Great advice. JONES: Yes. LLAMAS: Yes. headline: TODAY WITH HODA & JENNA for Dec 26, 2022, NBC
story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [10:00:17] HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS ANCHOR (voiceover): Today, get ready to be inspired. Donna shows up at the door of a beloved neighbor and gives him the ultimate sweet surprise. Plus, writer and poet Yung Pueblo. How his millions of followers are learning and healing from his every word. And the breast cancer survivor whose personal journey is touching and saving the lives of countless women. JENNA BUSH HAGER, NBC NEWS ANCHOR (voiceover): It`s TODAY WITH HODA -- KOTB: -- & JENNA. It all starts right now. HAGER: It all starts right now. KOTB (on camera): Hey, guys, happy day after Christmas. It`s Monday, December 26th. We hope that you all had a very merry one and a happy one. All the wrapping paper the bows and all that stuff tucked away. HAGER (on camera): Waking up with family still in the house. It`s -- what were they called this day in the U.K.? Boxing Day? KOTB: Boxing Day? They do? HAGER: Yes. I`m not sure why. KOTB: Oh, just like to decorative -- HAGER: But let`s celebrate Boxing Day. Why not? KOTB: OK. I like that. HAGER: And we`ve got an amazing show today that`s going to leave you feeling inspired and feeling good. Just as this day should. KOTB: Oh my God, this is -- this is our kind of show. HAGER: It sure is. KOTB: Because we love -- loves -- love things that feel like that. HAGER: Wait, in fact, can you just talk about the way you start your day? And the way you end your day? Because Henry is reading a book called Think Like A Monk by Jay Shetty. KOTB: Jay Shetty, yes. HAGER: And he says a lot of people think about the morning routine, but people forget about the end. KOTB: You know what`s funny? The morning routine I packed with inspirational readings and quotes and prayers and writing in my journal and all these kinds of things at night. I usually read and we have Yung Pueblo on today, a couple of lines from his book. And just before I close my eyes. Like last thing in, last thing in. I also try to say -- usually you think of like three things you`re grateful for. Yes, but a twist on that and this sounds vain, but it isn`t. Three things I appreciate about myself. Now, think about for right now, just freeze for a second. In this moment, what are three things you appreciate? Not that you`re grateful for? So, what is it that you`ve done that you appreciated? And it`s only for you, you`re not bragging. But what did you -- what have you done so far that you appreciate? And sometimes they`re small things like I gave my kids space, so that they could say what they wanted to say and then I received? OK, that`s the thing. And so, that`s the way -- HAGER: Yes. Or the way you handle situations. KOTB: Yes. Yes. HAGER: Yes, it`s so -- it`s so interesting, because I think we don`t even realize the negative stuff we say to ourselves, which is constant. Why did you do that? Why did you do that for? Why did you -- KOTB: I`m telling why (INAUDIBLE) should -- HAGER: You shouldn`t have said that. KOTB: Yes. HAGER: But -- so imagine just filling that time with? Oh, look, what you did there. You know, saying nice things. And I think it really does make a difference. KOTB: You know, Michelle Obama`s book that`s been out for a little bit is so beautifully written. But she talks about in one part, how we have a rectangular-sized shield that we put between us and the world. And she`s talking about the phone. HAGER: Oh, interesting. KOTB: And she says, what we`re doing every day is we are missing micro connections. You`re in the line at the bank, but I`m playing Candy Crush, so I don`t even look up to say hello, or I`m here and I`m doing something small. What your day -- she talked about how every day a micro connection and actually matters. It shows that we`re -- we may be different, but we`re human. But if you`re -- if there`s something in your ears and something in front of you, because people keep saying why are we drifting further apart? Tiny interactions that we would normally have. HAGER: Thank you. Yes. KOTB: Please, hi on the street. HAGER: The kind of smile that kind of makes you feel good. KOTB: Yes. Yes. HAGER: Wait, do you know -- so, when I first went back to work after having Mila, she`s 9, so about nine years ago, I got assigned the story. And I swear, it was like some sort of gift. Because the story was all about how basically kids are feeling like they`re not interesting. There was this doctor at Harvard who was studying what this -- what this does to a child. So, pretend you`re saying, Mommy, mommy -- KOTB: Hey, mom, mom, I want to tell you something. No, mom, mom, mom? HAGER: Hear. Hear. Hear. So, the words -- KOTB: Right. This is more important. HAGER: This is more important than this. KOTB: Than you. Than you. HAGER: And it was the best gift because what I realized is I was putting emphasis on work everything -- KOTB: I got to get this deal. Very important. HAGER: -- and you`ll (INAUDIBLE) instead of looking into my baby`s eye. KOTB: Yes. HAGER: And well, it`s not true. I mean, no mom thinks this is more interesting than their child. KOTB: Or, we don`t even realize -- we think how of just doing one quick thing, just one quick thing. HAGER: Anyway, that`s -- that could be a New Year`s resolution for a lot of people out there, and it`d be for mine. KOTB: Yes, yes. Me, too. [10:05:05] HAGER: OK. So, there`s research that recently was published in the Economic Times. It says humor at work actually accelerate creativity, motivation, and promoting productivity. KOTB: You know what, here`s the funny thing. I`m sitting next to this one. So, here`s the funny thing about you. Sometimes, I worry as we`re sitting here, because the things you say are so crazy and funny that I`ll just lose it instantly. But here`s the funny thing. I feel like there are ways -- there are ways of connection. HAGER: Yes. KOTB: For us, we have it. I think we have a deep kind of spiritual connection. But when you make me laugh, I feel so weirdly and crazily connected. Like I am -- sometimes I think about what you say much later in the day, and I`ll literally just be like, and goes what, I got nothing. It was something -- I can`t even explain. HAGER: You called me the other day. And you go, all I have to say is pirate and hung up. KOTB: You know why? Because I thought I was wearing a pair of cute black pants, black boots, but they didn`t meet in the middle. So, Jenna goes, hey, pirate. And literally, I was -- I just laughed, but that`s the whole thing. They say, it`s the whole thing. If you have them laughing, you have them listening. HAGER: That is such a good one. KOTB: And teachers who are -- yes, teachers who are -- who make kids laugh, kids lean in, they listen. HAGER: Totally. But laughing also is so much fun. I feel like that`s -- I mean, I`m coming up with all my New Year`s resolutions. Somebody, write this down. KOTB: What is it? HAGER: My other New Year`s resolution is to laugh more. KOTB: Yes. How? HAGER: Like why are we too busy? I mean, we laugh a lot because that`s our -- KOTB: Because we have -- and we also have space too. If we didn`t, if we were rushing through, you know, the whole -- HAGER: Rushing and doing this, and -- here`s your paper. Like, laugh instead, right? KOTB: Get in the next segment. I know. HAGER: Why don`t we just laugh more? KOTB: Yes, we do. HAGER: I mean, we do. In life, why don`t we -- KOTB: We all, collectively. OK, shall we see this video that`ll make us feel good. HAGER: Yes, yes. All right, this is the father of a bride in Jersey. So, the wedding videographer mic`d up the dad for his big walk down the aisle. So, let`s take a listen. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Nice and slow, honey. Look at his face. You see nothing but smiles. I love you, you know? Take care of her. Give me a hug, too. You`ll be fine, kiddo. I`ll be always by your side. You`ll never be alone, OK? (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB: Oh my gosh. HAGER: There were so few words yet they were so beautiful. KOTB: We were talking about laughing. HAGER: It`s good, now we`re crying. But you know what I think about crying? If you`re crying, you`re listening, too. KOTB: Yes, yes, yes. It works for both. All right, coming up, if you love a surprise we got a good one for you. HAGER: And Donna shows up unannounced to surprise a beloved neighbor right after this. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [10:10:00] HAGER: Now to our series, "KNOCK KNOCK SURPRISE!" And this is a surprise that`s going to fill your heart, for sure. KOTB: Yes. So, a few months ago, a viewer wrote in to tell us about her incredible neighbor of 20 years. His name is Ernie Mann. He lives in Rensselaer, New York. So, we sent Donna there to surprise him with something we knew he`d love. Check it out. DONNA FARIZAN, NBC NEWS HOST: This is so exciting, ladies. I`m here with Amy Mooney who nominated Ernie for National Good Neighbor Day. We`re walking up to his door right now. I`m going to leave you right there, Amy, OK? And I`m going up. I am -- we were hiding in the bushes for quite some time, a little bit nervous of what was going to happen, and how he`s going to react. Amy said that he`s going to be in shock. So, I`m going to knock on the door right now. And hopefully, Ernie will come out and be surprised. We can`t wait. There`s a crowd of over 30 here with us. This neighborhood loves him so much. And I don`t know how he`s going to react, but I`m hoping he`s going to be happy. So, let`s see what Ernie has to say. We`ve knock knocked the doors. Hi, Ernie, surprise! Ernie, come on out here. I`m Donna -- I`m Donna from the TODAY SHOW. And you are live. Come on over here with me, Ernie. It`s nice to meet you. You are so beloved as you can feel and see. And I don`t know if you know this, Ernie, but we can go right here. It is National Good Neighbor Day today. And we wanted to honor you because you are a pillar of this community. And you are just about the best neighbor that anyone could ask for. What`s going through your mind right now? ERNIE MANN, GOOD NEIGHBOR: Well, totally confused. FARIZAN: Well, let me fill you in a little bit more. Amy right here -- Amy right here nominated you. You are on live television on the TODAY SHOW right now. You can wave hi to Hoda and Jenna and millions of Americans if you want. We`re all here to honor you. MANN: Well, thank you very much. And if I had any influence in anything, I`d ask them if they`d please throw some fastballs to Aaron Judd. They walked in four times last night and a win. But anyway -- FARIZAN: So, Ernie, we know that Hoda and Jenna want to say something, too. So, we just are going to give you these earbuds, so you can listen to what`s going on. We know that you are so beloved and like a father figure to so many here. And I actually wanted to show you a little video on why Amy nominated you. Let`s take a look. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Ernie is a local legend in Rensselaer. He is not only a phenomenal neighbor, but a true hero in our community. He was a teacher for over 30 years, and he was also an active volunteer firefighter. He was our fire chief. [10:15:09] My kids would play wiffle ball in his backyard. Ernie`s like a dad to a lot of us, and he would do anything for any of us. Ernie and his wife, Jan moved into the neighborhood. That was almost 20 years ago. And unfortunately, Jan was stricken with ovarian cancer, and it took her way sooner than any of us thought. And Ernie was crushed. He`s not having the retirement he planned on with Jan. But he still celebrates life every day. He`s infamous for his mustache. His grandchildren can celebrate his mustache. They play in the snow, and they make his face on trees. We are Boston fans. Ernie is a Yankee fan. So, there`s a healthy rivalry going on. Ernie`s sense of humor can be summed up in a card that our daughter received at Johns Hopkins Hospital, he sent her a beautiful get well card and signed it Derek Jeter . Ernie is a person who has gone above and beyond, and now it`s time for us to honor him. He`s going to be so pissed at me. You have no idea. (END VIDEO CLIP) FARIZAN: Is that true? How do you feel right now? MANN: I`m overwhelmed, honestly. FARIZAN: I`ll take -- I`ll take these out. I know -- MANN: Totally, I don`t know what to say. I don`t know -- I -- my response was, who the hell is at my door at this time of day? FARIZAN: It was us. There are a lot of -- a lot of iterations of the mustache everywhere. And I know your late wife Jan would be so proud of all you`ve done today. MANN: Thank you so much. Thank you. FARIZAN: And all the love you`re receiving today. MANN: Thank you so much. FARIZAN: Have you always loved Rensselaer this much? MANN: Yes, I have. Yes. My father was born in Rensselaer. And before it was Rensselaer, actually. And now, I`ve lived through all my life. And it`s a wonderful city. People are just great. I taught 33 years into schools, and then the fire department now pushing 60 years. And it`s just a wonderful town. FARIZAN: Well, thank you for all that you do. You`re such a great representation of not only calm but a good neighbor. MANN: Thank you so much. FARIZAN: And you know, I wanted you to put the earbuds in one more time because I heard Ernie that you are a big Yankees fan. Is that right? MANN: Yes, that`s true. FARIZAN: So, well, in honor of that, I think there`s a member of the team that wanted to say hello to you if that`s OK, let`s take a listen. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) NESTOR CORTES: Nestor Cortes here with the New York Yankees . I just want to congratulate you on being a good neighbor. We`ve heard all about you and what you`ve do -- and what you`ve done with the community. By the way, we have a special gift coming for you. So, stay tuned. And go Yankees . (END VIDEO CLIP) FARIZAN: Well, I know that you just saw Nestor Cortes, Jr. through the screen. But you know what, can we just grab some Yankees swag? OK, this is for you. I think you`re going to need it because, Ernie, we are getting you four tickets to Yankee Stadium, so you can go see Nestor (INAUDIBLE) and you have a lot of people to choose from to take with you. How do you feel? MANN: I`m, honest to God, I`m overwhelmed. And I totally didn`t see any of this coming. I don`t know -- FARIZAN: Well, you know, thank you so much for being a great neighbor. MANN: Well, I`ve had great neighbors around me. It`s been pretty easy. All the people around me, they`re wonderful people. FARIZAN: As we send it back to Hoda and Jenna, is there one piece of advice you would give people to become a better neighbor? MANN: If you just look out for each other, if you look and see if somebody`s up against it, try to help them a little bit. You can do it quietly. You don`t have to make a big fuss. And if just people are nicer to each other all over. It`s easy to do. FARIZAN: Thank you, Ernie. It`s easy to do with you. KOTB: Oh my gosh, how much do we love Earnie. HAGER: We love Earnie. He`s such a sweet, sweet man, and what a great group of neighbors, a beautiful community. KOTB: Incredible. Incredible. Coming up next, a mother of two who wouldn`t let breast cancer beat her, and now she`s helping other women get a fighting chance coming up after this. [10:20:00] (COMMERCIAL BREAK) HAGER: All morning long, we`re celebrating people whose stories inspire us to live our very best life. KOTB: Breast cancer survivor Ricki Fairley is one of those people. After defying the odds, she created a brand new life for herself with a very important mission. Take a look. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) RICKI FAIRLEY, BREAST CANCER SURVIVOR: I try to like let everything go and just paddle and just feel the water and see that -- feel the sun or the wind. Feel God around me. KOTB (voiceover): Ricki Fairley starts most of our days like this, alone and at peace on the Chesapeake Bay. But this mother of two didn`t always know how to slow down. Like most caregivers, Ricki was constantly on the go. FAIRLEY: I was a crazy, busy typical mom, working mom. I actually had been married for 30 years, and I was the breadwinner for our family, traveling every week on the road. KOTB: After a routine mammogram, the words triple negative breast cancer stopped her in her tracks. FAIRLEY: My doctor said we found five spots on your chest wall. You are now metastatic. You have two years to live. Get your affairs in order. We don`t have anything for you. And I said, well, I can`t really die right now. I have a daughter at Dartmouth. I have to pay for her tuition. So, me, you and gotten some drugs or something. We got to work this out. KOTB: It was a long road of surgeries, chemotherapy, radiation, and experimental drugs, but it worked. And Ricki was cancer free. She decided to quit her old life and start fresh. [10:25:03] FAIRLEY: I knew I had to get rid of all the cancers in my life. I divorced my husband of 30 years. I quit my business partner of 10 years. I sold my house in Alpharetta, Georgia with a pool and two acres, and I moved to my little one-bedroom condo on the beach. KOTB: She also did a lot of research and learned about the disparity in breast cancer for black women. FAIRLEY: This disease for black women is a different disease. And now, we have a growing body of data that validates that a black breast cancer cell looks different from a white one. We have a 41 percent higher mortality rate than white women. We have a 39 percent higher recurrence rate of breast cancer than white woman, which is crazy. KOTB: So, with her new home, her new fiance and her new way of life came a new purpose, a nonprofit called Touch: The Black Breast Cancer Alliance. KOTB: 11 years after she was told she was going to die, Ricki is still cancer free and has been able to watch her oldest daughter get married and have a family of her own. FAIRLEY: Your piece is non-negotiable. Take care of yourself, check your breasts, give yourself a minute, give yourself a pause. It`s OK to say no. So many women that with --that had what I had didn`t make it. And I know that God left me here to do this work to be an advocate for other women. It`s my purpose. (END VIDEOTAPE) KOTB (on camera): Ricki, I mean, we are in awe of you. Your purpose came with that horrible diagnosis. A huge change. You made so many changes that you`re probably too afraid to make your whole life. What -- was there ever a point of trepidation? Should I divorce my husband, change all these things because of this -- of what happened to you? FAIRLEY: No. There was no trepidation. I knew -- I knew in my spirit that I had to save my life. And I just went for it. I didn`t even think twice about it. And people said, are you crazy? are you sure you should do all this at one time? Do you want to think about it? I said, no, I have to go now. HAGER: You know, the best thing about this is that you had the second life and you`re using it to help other women. You -- those statistics that we heard in the piece are unacceptable. You could have just read those and thought, OK, but instead, you`re fighting them. And that just seems like an incredible mission. FAIRLEY: I work for my granddaughters. I don`t want them to ever think about breast cancer, and we have a lot of work to do to save black women. And I don`t -- I don`t want anybody to die of breast cancer. But we deserve mortality rate parity. KOTB: Well, I thought what you said after the diagnosis was like you, the doctor, me, God, medicine, whatever, we all do -- we`re all going to have to work together on this one. You sound like your faith was unshakable throughout. FAIRLEY: It was. I -- you know, faith is my spiritual gift. I know that God left me here to do this work. And I`m on a mission to try to change how we think about it. HAGER: Well, Ricki, we are impressed with you if that`s not obvious. But also, Thrive Cosmetics, they told us they were so inspired by the work that you do to eradicate black breast cancer. But guess what, they`re donating $10,000 to Touch to continue the efforts that you put in in everything you do. FAIRLEY: Oh, wow, that`s so awesome. HAGER: Will that be able to make a difference? FAIRLEY: That will be awesome. You know, we have this movement called When We Trial. Whenwetrial.org to educate black woman about clinical trials, so we can get better drugs, so I will put it to work today. HAGER: Oh, awesome. Ricki, we love you. KOTB: You`re unbelievable. You`re unbelievable. Wow, what a gift for us. Thank you so much. HAGER: Thank you. Thank you. Thank you so much. FAIRLEY: That`s such a blessing. Thank you so much. KOTB: Wow, for us too. PUEBLO: Yes. HAGER: Like -- and I love that you have said, it`s OK to feel -- PUEBLO: Totally. Yes. HAGER: It`s OK to have those emotions, and you have to. PUEBLO: You know, it`s a bit of a risk and but it worked out for us. KOTB: Well, I have your book by my bedside, it`s one of those you can open up read one beautiful line and go to sleep and sleep really well. So -- HAGER: She actually goes to bed with your words in her head every night. KOTB: Yes. PUEBLO: Wow. HAGER: And then make her feel lighter. PUEBLO: That`s a big honor. KOTB: Big for me too. Thank you. HAGER: And then make her feel lighter. And I think if you want that light, it`s here. KOTB: Yes. And you got to get the book, Lighter. And also, your other two books are amazing. I like all three, but get this one because it`s new. (END VIDEOTAPE) KOTB: By the way, since that segment aired Yung Pueblo`s book Lighter reached number one on the New York Times bestsellers list. headline: TODAY WITH HODA & JENNA for Dec 26, 2022, NBC
story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [10:00:17] HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS ANCHOR (voiceover): Today, get ready to be inspired. Donna shows up at the door of a beloved neighbor and gives him the ultimate sweet surprise. Plus, writer and poet Yung Pueblo. How his millions of followers are learning and healing from his every word. And the breast cancer survivor whose personal journey is touching and saving the lives of countless women. JENNA BUSH HAGER, NBC NEWS ANCHOR (voiceover): It`s TODAY WITH HODA -- KOTB: -- & JENNA. It all starts right now. HAGER: It all starts right now. KOTB (on camera): Hey, guys, happy day after Christmas. It`s Monday, December 26th. We hope that you all had a very merry one and a happy one. All the wrapping paper the bows and all that stuff tucked away. HAGER (on camera): Waking up with family still in the house. It`s -- what were they called this day in the U.K.? Boxing Day? KOTB: Boxing Day? They do? HAGER: Yes. I`m not sure why. KOTB: Oh, just like to decorative -- HAGER: But let`s celebrate Boxing Day. Why not? KOTB: OK. I like that. HAGER: And we`ve got an amazing show today that`s going to leave you feeling inspired and feeling good. Just as this day should. KOTB: Oh my God, this is -- this is our kind of show. HAGER: It sure is. KOTB: Because we love -- loves -- love things that feel like that. HAGER: Wait, in fact, can you just talk about the way you start your day? And the way you end your day? Because Henry is reading a book called Think Like A Monk by Jay Shetty. KOTB: Jay Shetty, yes. HAGER: And he says a lot of people think about the morning routine, but people forget about the end. KOTB: You know what`s funny? The morning routine I packed with inspirational readings and quotes and prayers and writing in my journal and all these kinds of things at night. I usually read and we have Yung Pueblo on today, a couple of lines from his book. And just before I close my eyes. Like last thing in, last thing in. I also try to say -- usually you think of like three things you`re grateful for. Yes, but a twist on that and this sounds vain, but it isn`t. Three things I appreciate about myself. Now, think about for right now, just freeze for a second. In this moment, what are three things you appreciate? Not that you`re grateful for? So, what is it that you`ve done that you appreciated? And it`s only for you, you`re not bragging. But what did you -- what have you done so far that you appreciate? And sometimes they`re small things like I gave my kids space, so that they could say what they wanted to say and then I received? OK, that`s the thing. And so, that`s the way -- HAGER: Yes. Or the way you handle situations. KOTB: Yes. Yes. HAGER: Yes, it`s so -- it`s so interesting, because I think we don`t even realize the negative stuff we say to ourselves, which is constant. Why did you do that? Why did you do that for? Why did you -- KOTB: I`m telling why (INAUDIBLE) should -- HAGER: You shouldn`t have said that. KOTB: Yes. HAGER: But -- so imagine just filling that time with? Oh, look, what you did there. You know, saying nice things. And I think it really does make a difference. KOTB: You know, Michelle Obama`s book that`s been out for a little bit is so beautifully written. But she talks about in one part, how we have a rectangular-sized shield that we put between us and the world. And she`s talking about the phone. HAGER: Oh, interesting. KOTB: And she says, what we`re doing every day is we are missing micro connections. You`re in the line at the bank, but I`m playing Candy Crush, so I don`t even look up to say hello, or I`m here and I`m doing something small. What your day -- she talked about how every day a micro connection and actually matters. It shows that we`re -- we may be different, but we`re human. But if you`re -- if there`s something in your ears and something in front of you, because people keep saying why are we drifting further apart? Tiny interactions that we would normally have. HAGER: Thank you. Yes. KOTB: Please, hi on the street. HAGER: The kind of smile that kind of makes you feel good. KOTB: Yes. Yes. AYANNA SHAH, PRESIDENT, SECOND SERVE: Tennis has taught me so many lessons and I think the biggest one is learning how to push through obstacles. HAGER: And since 2019 their nonprofit organization Second Serve has been working to give kids around the world equitable access to tennis. AMANI SHAH: When I was 10 years old was when I really fell in love with the sport. AYANNA SHAH: The relationships that I`ve built through tennis have been just amazing. AMANI SHAH: Historically, tennis has been deemed an elitist sport because of its very high-cost entry. AYANNA SHAH: Second Serve redistributes new and gently used tennis equipment all around the world. Our mission is to create greater access, inclusion, and diversity within the sport. One of my personal favorite donations was to a young girl in Nigeria named Nana Rosie (PH). UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: I started playing tennis since I was three years old. AMANI SHAH: Nana spends four to five hours every day playing tennis and her dedication is really an inspiration for us. HAGER: Ayanna and Amani tap teams across the U.S. to make this all happen. AMANI SHAH: Our team has grown to over 90 different high school team members all across the U.S. We`ve been able to redistribute over 20,000 items in over 26 states and 14 different countries. EMMA HIGUCHI, COO, SECOND SERVE: What I was drawn to is it was a -- it`s a youth-led organization. We always have monthly meetings. Just hearing their great ideas is really great and hopefully, we can make those ideas come reality. SUSAN PRATT, TENNIS COACH, ORANGE GLEN HIGH SCHOOL: The Shah sisters of Second Serve have been an inspiration to me and also to our high school tennis team. It`s a school of 91 percent economically disadvantaged kids. Having a tennis racquet gives them that sense of ownership. DIANNA, ORANGE GLEN HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT: At first I couldn`t really hit but now I can do like everything. PRATT: Now she`s competing. She`s our number one player. I have seen her build a sense of confidence. I stopped. HAGER: Inspired to do more in their own backyard, the team started Serve Escondido. AMANI SHAH: We provide free tennis lessons for under-resourced kids in our own hometown of San Diego. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Good job. HAGER: And in the spirit of giving back, we had a little surprise for Second Serve. AMANI SHAH: Second Serve has done incredible work to make the game of tennis accessible to all. To help continue that work, Wilson is donating 100 tennis rackets and 50 pairs of youth sneakers to Second Serve. AYANNA SHAH: Oh my gosh. That`s incredible. Oh! Second Serves` mission of enhancing the lives of underserved children by fostering a love for tennis is inspirational and empowering, to support that mission Athleta is donating 100 girls` tennis dresses to Second Serve. Oh, my God. AMANI SHAH: Thank you so much. This is awesome. It`s just really special to see that other people support this vision of greater access and greater diversity for all kids. When I`m on the tennis court, I`ve experienced that what you believe is really what you can achieve. When you`re about to serve when you`re about to hit a ball if you can visualize that ball going exactly to your target. That`s often exactly what happens. (END VIDEOTAPE) HAGER: The Shah sisters are going to take over the world. A big thank you to Wilson and Athleta for helping us with that surprise. KOTB: Yes, that was awesome. We`re back right after this. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [10:56:58] KOTB: Heart. We hope we let you feel good today. Tomorrow we`re going to meet some of our favorite foodies. headline: The Today Show for December 8, 2022, NBC
story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [08:00:00] HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS TODAY, CO-ANCHOR: It`s 8:00 on "TODAY." Coming up, flu fears. New concerns over medication shortages as cases spike from coast to coast. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: There`s hardly anything to choose from. (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB: Coming up, what you can do to ensure your family is prepared this flu season. Plus, breast cancer breakthrough. The just-released study sparking hope for women with breast cancer who want to start a new family. What the promising new data shows about a safe path forward. And Garten`s variety. The Barefoot Contessa herself, Ina Garten, joins us for a full hour to help spruce up our holiday tables, from a new spin on some tasty treats to becoming the host with the most. Plus, a glimpse into some of our most treasured traditions. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) CROWD: Three, two -- yahey. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Blast off. (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB: We`ve got a fun-filled hour ahead with a few surprises along the way. Today, Thursday, December 8, 2022. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Best friends. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: And "TODAY" super fans. CROWD: From Parkersburg, West Virginia. CROWD: From Pullman, Washington. CROWD: And Lynwood, Illinois. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: From Hagerstown, Maryland. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Celebrating our 25th anniversary. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Friends for 20 years. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: From El Paso, Texas. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Here with my grandson. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: From Mechanicsville, Virginia. CROWD: Hello from Woodbine, Iowa. CROWD: And Cincinnati, Ohio. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Celebrating Vicky`s birthday. CROWD: From Baton Rouge. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Here to experience a magic. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Of Christmas in New York. CROWD: From Mizpah, Minnesota. (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB: Welcome back. How do we say thank you for coming out -- SAVANNAH GUTHRIE, NBC NEWS TODAY, CO-ANCHOR: I know. KOTB: -- every morning? This crowd, it`s like six people thick. It`s a big crowd. We cannot wait to get outside and visit with everybody in just a bit. But what do you say we get to our news at 8:00? CRAIG MELVIN, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Yes. KOTB: An early surge in flu cases is sending more Americans to the hospital and it`s actually causing pharmacies to run out of both prescription and over-the-counter treatments. NBC Sam brock has the latest on how long this might last and what you should do in case your drugstore shelves are empty. Sam, good morning. SAM BROCK, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Yes. Hoda, good morning. The mere fact that the flu season has arrived weeks in advance, as you said, has put parents in quite a crunch, pretty much across the board from antibiotics to antivirals. It`s true in Coral Gables, Florida, where I am, in San Francisco, California, Detroit, Michigan. All over the country. Now, the owner of University Pharmacist here tells me that amoxicillin right now, she has, about, maybe four or five patients worth of supplies left here. This is so important, it`s so critical because it`s the preferred antibiotic for kids. It`s a little bit milder, fewer side effects. That`s just one example. She wants to order more, cannot right now. Check out the store shelves. When it comes to decongestants, you see some Mucinex but the rest of the shelf here is empty. Robitussin, Sudafed they were down here, that`s gone as well. As far as anti-inflammatories for kids, Tylenol and Advil, there`s empty spaces on the shelf for that as well. All of it is unavailable. Now, the ASHP is a pharmacy group that tracks short supplies for drugs. They have right now, Hoda, some 260 drugs nationally that are short at the moment that includes Tamiflu, which is the most popular drug for treating the flu for kids, certainly, for adults as well. The issue with Tamiflu says one of their manufacturers, they have enough supply. They said it`s available for pharmacies to buy, but the owner here tells me it now cost three times of what it did just a few weeks ago. So, that anecdotally, is something that we`re seeing on the ground. This problem could go on for a number of weeks, well into the holidays. One of the advice -- pieces of advice doctors have for you, make you`re your pediatricians office contacts the pharmacy ahead of time to see if they have a drug in stock and to ask if there`s a viable alternative if there`s not. But parents right now are having to get creative as they go through this period where everybody is getting sick. Hoda, back to you. KOTB: Yes, happening in my neighborhood, too. All right. Sam Brock for us. Sam, thank you. GUTHRIE: For the first time in four decades, journalists and other employees at " The New York Times " are staging a large-scale walkout. The 24-hour strike by more than 1,000 members of the news gilded New York started just after midnight. The union says it lost patience with contract talks that have gone on for two years. A spokesperson for the "The Times" denied the talks were at an impasse and said it was disappointing that the union had taken what she called an extreme action. Negotiations have stalled over wages and remote work rules. MELVIN: A new study has found that women who`ve been treated for breast cancer may be able to pause their follow-up medications long enough to have a baby. After treatment, patients often take drugs to suppress their hormones for up to 10 years, but those drugs can also make it hard to conceive. [08:05:00] The new research led by Dr. Ann Partridge looked at how to balance the need for drug therapy with the desire to complete a family. And it found that within three years of pausing their medications, women had no greater risk of their cancers returning than those who stayed on the drugs, and about two-thirds were able to conceive and have a child. GUTHRIE: Well, grownups, who can`t recall third grade English lessons, can probably still sing every word of the "Schoolhouse Rock" cartoon that aired on Saturday mornings in the `70s and `80s. Well, George Newall, the man who helped create those classis tunes has passed away. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Conjunction junction what`s your function. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Hooking up words and phrases and clauses. (END VIDEO CLIP) GUTHRIE: I mean, we`re just singing it right here. KOTB: Yes. Uh-huh. MELVIN: Uh-huh. GUTHRIE: Those cartoons had a generation of kids about math and science and civics and grammar. Newall was an advertising pro. He composed all of those songs including "I`m Just a Bill on Capitol Hill." Remember that one? KOTB: Uh-huh. GUTHRIE: "Three is a Magic Number", he got the idea when a colleague with children asked about putting multiplication tables to music. George Newall was 88 years old. What a legacy. KOTB: Wow. Indeed. Wow. All right. Guys, would you like a little "Morning Boost"? GUTHRIE: Yes. MELVIN: Yes. KOTB: You got it. As you probably know, a white elephant party, it`s when you get together with your friends and you exchange silly gifts, usually just for kicks. So, Baylor University volleyball player Lauren Briseno never imagined she would -- what she would unwrap during their white elephant party that her coach hosted for the team. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) LAUREN BRISENO, BAYLOR UNIVERSITY VOLLEYBALL PLAYER: Hear ye, hear ye. It is with great exclamation that this proclamation be read. Due to unwavering diligence and determination for relentlessness and execution of incredible skills at the highest levels. For you (ph) of this year proclamation has hereby earned yourself a full scholarship. (END VIDEO CLIP) MELVIN: Oh, wow. GUTHRIE: Wow. KOTB: Lauren is a sophomore, by the way. She was a walk-on on the volleyball team. That was a surprise scholarship. She said she was eternally grateful. I mean, you think you`re getting one of those white elephant gifts. GUTHRIE: I know. KOTB: And you get one of that. GUTHRIE: Exactly. It sure beats the fridge magnet or whatever. MELVIN: Yes. GUTHRIE: All right. Guys, next, this is the next best thing to actually be invited to Ina Garten`s house. KOTB: Yes. GUTHRIE: She is here. She`s in our house, and giving all of her secrets for throwing a memorable holiday party from the moment your guests walk through the door to a parting gift they will never forget. Ina, the hostess with the most will host this show. MELVIN: Yes. KOTB: Yes. INA GARTEN, BAREFOOT CONTESSA HOST: We are going to have such a great time. GUTHRIE: We are, my friend. We`re back after this. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [08:10:00] ANNOUNCER: From NBC News, this is a Special Report. Here`s Savannah Guthrie and Hoda Kotb. GUTHRIE: Good morning, everybody. We are following breaking news at this hour out of Russia. Nearly 10 months after her arrest and incarceration there, WNBA star Brittney Griner is headed home. KOTB: Yes. Breaking and welcome news. Russia has agreed to a prisoner swap with the U.S. We`re going to go straight to NBC`s Chief Foreign Affairs Correspondent, Andrea Mitchell, she has these breaking details. Andrea, what can you tell us? ANDREA MITCHELL, NBC NEWS CHIEF WASHINGTON CORRESPONDENT: Good morning, Savannah and Hoda. Well, according to a senior administration official, Brittney Griner is free after 294 days in Russian captivity. The last month spent in Russia`s notoriously harsh penal colonies. She was traded for Russian arms dealer Viktor Bout who Vladimir Putin has been trying to get back and had served 11 years of a 25-year sentence in the U.S. President Biden signed off on the trade even though it meant leaving another American businessman, Paul Whelan, behind bars in Russia. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) MITCHELL (voiceover): Over the weekend, Secretary of State, Antony Blinken , saying the U.S. has been actively engaged in discussions with Russia about a possible prisoner swap to free Brittney Griner and Paul Whelan. ANTONY BLINKEN, U.S. SECRETARY OF STATE: We have to see if the engagements that we`ve had, the discussions that we had produced an actual result. MITCHELL (voiceover): Griner, the 32-year-old WNBA superstar has spent nearly 10 months in Russian custody. Arrested at a Moscow airport in February. She admitted to bringing less than a gram of medicinal cannabis into the country but said she never intended to break any law. Her plight sparked an outpouring from her family, teammates and fans. Griner`s wife, Cherelle. CHERELLE GRINER, BRITTNEY GRINER`S WIFE: I`m frustrated that my wife is not going to get justice. I know you all are frustrated, too, that`s why you`re here. MITCHELL (voiceover): Sentenced to nine years in prison, Griner appealed, pleading for leniency from behind bars. BRITTNEY GRINER, WNBA PLAYER IMPRISONED IN RUSSIA: This has been very traumatic experience waiting for this day. MITCHELL (voiceover): But she was denied. President Biden last month. JOE BIDEN , U.S. PRESIDENT: I`m telling you, I am determined to get her home and get her home safely. Along with others, I might add. MITCHELL (voiceover): The other American held by Russia will not be coming home. Paul Whelan, a former marine, a businessman, detained four years ago is serving a 16-year prison sentence after being accused of spying, which the U.S. strongly denies. Whelan`s family later raised concerns about his safety, which I asked the secretary of state about last week. BLINKEN: We`re working to bring him home, to bring Brittney Griner home. But this is, again, what we see Russia doing in terms of abusing the very basic understandings that countries have had when it comes to having access to our citizens who are being detained. (END VIDEO CLIP) MITCHELL (on camera): Those familiar with these very hard negotiations say that the Russians absolutely refused to release Paul Whelan without getting a Russian spy in return. But the U.S. insists it does not have any Russian spies in U.S. custody. So, the administration says, it had no one to trade to meet that Russian demand. And again, the U.S. maintains that Paul Whelan is wrongfully detained. He`s a businessman, not a spy. And just now we also got a statement from the group that has been campaigning for all of these hostages to be released from all over the world, actually, saying Paul Whelan has been let down and left behind by -- at least three times, by two American presidents. He deserves better from his government and our campaign implores President Biden to urgently secure Paul`s immediate return using all tools available. We understand the president will be speaking shortly or later this morning. GUTHRIE: Yes. Andrea, thank you very much for the breaking news. Brittney Griner has been freed. Paul Whelan left behind. Let`s go to Chief White House Correspondent Peter Alexander at the White House. What`s the word there, Peter? PETER ALEXANDER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT AND WEEKEND TODAY CO-ANCHOR: Savannah, we do expect to hear from President Biden at 8:30, so 15 minutes from now. And we have just learned that Cherelle Griner, Brittney Griner`s wife, is right now in the Oval Office here at the white house. She`s behind closed doors with the president. [08:15:00] The two of them were able to speak by phone earlier this morning with Brittney Griner after she was returned to U.S. custody. And then as we understand it, Cherelle was able to have a private conversation with her wife, Brittney, from the president`s study. But this concludes for the Griner family what has just been a very distressing situation over the course of the last 10 months. The president has said this was a top priority. He had exchanged a letter with Griner in the past who wrote him, over the summer, saying that she was terrified she would be there forever in Russian custody. The good news this morning that the White House will certainly be celebrating today is the release of Brittney Griner. And again, to repeat, Cherelle Griner`s, the president`s -- is in the Oval Office with the president right now and had an opportunity to speak alongside the president with her wife just this morning. Savannah and Hoda. KOTB: All right. Peter Alexander, thank you so much. We are going to continue to keep a close eye on the story all morning long. We`re going to bring you updates. And of course, we`ll have coverage on "NBC Nightly News" and all day on "NBC News NOW". GUTHRIE: For now, many of our stations will return to the "TODAY" show in New York. This is Savannah Guthrie and Hoda Kotb. Good day. 8:16. We want to turn now to Dylan and get a check of the weather. She is aboard a ship, are you not? Oh, where are you now? DYLAN DREYER, NBC NEWS 3RD HOUR OF TODAY CO-HOST AND METEOROLOGIST: I am, but I brought you inside now to show you some of the extravagance here in an atrium. This staircase made of Swarovski crystals, I mean, because that`s what you need on a cruise ship after all. But let`s take a look at what`s going on outside. Here in the northeast, it is a little bit chilly but I`d say seasonable for this time of year. It`s really down through the Ohio River Valley where we`ll see a lot of that rain move in today, heavy at times. And the snow is going to move into the Upper Midwest. Temperatures, still very warm, especially down along the Gulf Coast where we`ll likely break high temperatures today. Although it is going to be quite chilly across the Northern Plains. Highs only in the teens and 20s. That`s a look at the weather across the country. Now, here`s a peek out your window. (LOCAL NEWS) DREYER: And that`s your latest forecast. Back to you guys. GUTHRIE: All right. Dylan, thank you. Well, back in Studio 1A, we have gathered to kick off our series "Ina`s Holiday Table". And we are at Ina`s holiday table right now. We`re all getting a special invite to her home as Ina Garten co-hosts this entire hour with us. KOTB: Yes. MELVIN: We are so excited. GARTEN: It`s crazy. KOTB: OK. First of all, Ina, how does it feel to be a co-anchor? GARTEN: Thank you. It`s just so fun and scary. KOTB: Well, you`re going to be amazing because I love -- you make everything simple. You`re going to make our holiday season a little brighter, a little warmer without the fuss. You got friends. But your keyword you keep talking about is simple, which is what we love the most. GARTEN: It`s so important. That`s exactly right, Hoda. I`m so excited to be here with all of you. The holidays can be so stressful. What do you make? How do you entertain? It can feel totally overwhelming, even for me. So, I`m here to show you how to simplify it and actually enjoy the holidays. How is that for a newbie? GUTHRIE: I love that. CARSON DALY, NBC NEWS HOST: Love it. GARTEN: So, before we get to drinking the cranberry martinis. MELVIN: Do it, Carson. GARTEN: Let`s hear how all of you like to celebrate the holiday season. CROWD: Cheers. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) DALY: If you get an invite to the Daly house, you`re going to be transformed right into the true spirit of Christmas. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: It`s the most wonderful time of the year. GUTHRIE: I have become a holiday decor person. I admit it. I`m buying cute little things with my name on it and the kids` names. KOTB: We have a beautiful Christmas tree that we love. CROWD: Three, two -- yahey. UNIDENTIFIED FEMALE: Blast off. KOTB: It`s only got decorations on the bottom because that`s where the kids could reach. MELVIN: I can`t imagine the holidays without Christmas music. I`ve been playing all of my favorites. And my son`s favorite Christmas song is the Donny Hathaway classic. KOTB: I`m going to be totally honest, I don`t host or entertain that much. I mean, if someone comes over, I`m like, I think we have cookies. Are you OK with this? DALY: I`m controversial with my Christmas holiday hosting duties because I`m a fun of eggnog. And I feel like eggnog is getting a bad rep these days. So, if you like eggnog, you`re always welcome in our house. MELVIN: When my wife twists my arm and we actually have people over for the holidays, I make a nice big cocktail. It`s sort of my take on a hot toddy and she makes everything else. GUTHRIE: I love having people over. Nothing formal. Just come on by. Everybody`s in their cozy sweaters. Everyone`s happy. It`s just beautiful time of year. (END VIDEO CLIP) GARTEN: Savannah, you said you like to have like a free-wheeling -- GUTHRIE: Yes. GARTEN: -- like a holiday party. GUTHRIE: Crazy. GARTEN: People just come and go. GUTHRIE: I do. GARTEN: You know what I love to do, I like to have a surprise guest. GUTHRIE: Yes. [08:20:00] GARTEN: Somebody everybody just adores and they`re just so happy to see. GUTHRIE: Someone that everyone will like. GARTEN: It has to be someone everyone will like. GUTHRIE: OK. KOTB: OK. GARTEN: And so, I invited a surprise guest -- KOTB: Who? GARTEN: -- to our party. KOTB: Who? MELVIN: Who is it? GARTEN: And I think he`s waiting in the wings. Willie Geist, are you here? GUTHRIE: Oh, my God. Drake (ph)? Oh, it`s Willie. KOTB: Willie -- WILLIE GEIST, SUNDAY TODAY, HOST: Are you disappointed it was me? GUTHRIE: I thought it was going to be Beyonce. DALY: I thought Santa was coming out. KOTB: Hi, Willie. GEIST: Great to see you. GARTEN: It`s so good to see you. GEIST: I bought you some coffee mugs for you and Jeffrey. But also can be used for cranberry martinis. GARTEN: Oh, yes. GEIST: Yes, yes, yes. GUTHRIE: Hi, Willie. KOTB: Come sit with us. GARTEN: How great is that? Did I nail that? KOTB: Why is willie your go-to guest, because he does bring the fun. DALY: He is a great guest. KOTB: Yes, he really is. GARTEN: He`s a funster. KOTB: He`s a funster? GARTEN: We had such a good -- GEIST: We`ve had some fun. GARTEN: We`ve had some fun together. KOTB: Really? GARTEN: Yes, really. Now, that`s really suggestive to say. GUTHRIE: Wow. Jeffrey was there. KOTB: Jeffrey was there and your wife, Christina, was there. GEIST: Exactly. Yes. We drink together, yes. GARTEN: So, we had a really good time together. So, I have so many questions to ask you about holiday. KOTB: OK. GARTEN: And it`s hard. It`s really stressful. And I try to keep it simple. And I -- so, Willie, what do you like to do? You like to make cocktails, right? GEIST: I like a cocktail. I like a big tent, like you, guys. Wide open, everybody come over, put some drinks out, put good music on. I just want everybody to have fun and be relaxed. KOTB: Yes. GUTHRIE: Yes. GARTEN: You know, one of the things I want, when people arrive at the door, I want all of your senses engaged. KOTB: Uh-huh. GARTEN: I want something delicious to eat, like caramelized pecans. Great music. And you guys are talking about having great music -- KOTB: Yes. DALY: Yes. GARTEN: -- and, you know, just really gorgeous -- GUTHRIE: On the fireplace -- DALY: Open firepit. GEIST: Fire, yes. GARTEN: -- gorgeous house. GUTHRIE: Are those your five senses, Ina, like do you kind of -- GARTEN: You want to smell something wonderful. So, it can be, like -- sometimes if I get an apple pie, I`ll just put it in the oven, even though it`s from the bakery. So, it smells like apple pie, doesn`t it? KOTB: Wow. That is brilliant. GARTEN: What are the other things that, like, smell great? KOTB: Cookies. GUTHRIE: You know, I love a candle. And Al bought us all the Harlem candle company. MELVIN: Yes. GUTHRIE: That green candle. And I`ve been lighting it all season and it`s just -- GARTEN: So, when you walk in, it just feels like a party. GUTHRIE: It smells so good. KOTB: It feels like cozy, cozy. GARTEN: Or, like if you have a fireplace, you can have a fire and it`s both smell and the fire but also the crackling. KOTB: Ina, I mean, I love Willie. I think he`s a great guest. GEIST: We can do better. KOTB: No. GUTHRIE: No. DALY: You`re good guest, but on TV you`re a terrible guest. KOTB: But I think there is someone who I think you adore -- I think you`ve been trying to get together with her for a while. It hasn`t been able to work out. GUTHRIE: Yes, schedule. KOTB: But you know what, today it will. GARTEN: Who? KOTB: Misty Copeland. MELVIN: No. KOTB: Will you please come out? MELVIN: Oh, I love that. GARTEN: A surprise guest. Oh, I`m so happy to see you. MISTY COPELAND, BALLET DANCER, AMERICAN BALLET THEATRE: I`m so happy I can be here and see you. KOTB: Hi, Misty. GUTHRIE: Hi, Misty. DALY: Hi, Misty. MELVIN: Hi, Misty. GUTHRIE: Have a seat at Ina`s table. COPELAND: Oh, thank you. KOTB: There you go, Ina. GUTHRIE: Ina, are you shocked? GARTEN: I`m shocked. KOTB: Now, tell us about -- you wanted Misty to be your guest. GARTEN: Well, she is. She was my guest on -- we spent a day together at my house. And we cooked together -- COPELAND: Yes, we did. GARTEN: -- and we talked about your unbelievable career. I mean, this is like the most amazing -- KOTB: Is she not amazing? GARTEN: Just amazing. We won`t talk about her while she`s here. GUTHRIE: Misty, do you like to host? Is that something like -- COPELAND: I do. GUTHRIE: Yes. COPELAND: And I -- we`ve talked about it. But I learned so much -- you know, moving to New York City when I was 17 years old and learning to host and to cook by watching Ina. GARTEN: You know, one of the things I think we all forget in hosting is about the people. MELVIN: Yes. GARTEN: It`s not about the food. KOTB: OK. GARTEN: I mean, you want the food to be good. But you can just go out and get, like, apple cider and put it on the stove and have cookies and -- I mean, your -- you`re always nervous about hosting. KOTB: Can I be honest? MELVIN: Yes. KOTB: Guys, you`re going to think I`m crazy. I don`t think I`ve ever hosted a party at my house. GARTEN: Just -- GUTHRIE: What? MELVIN: No. KOTB: Other than a birthday party for my kids or something or my sister -- GUTHRIE: And you were born to party. What`s this? DALY: You`re like Willie. You`re a great guest at other parties. You probably make the rounds during the holiday. KOTB: I do that. But I -- I don`t know if whether I`m nervous or I feel like -- I don`t know if it would be good or will people be bored? GEIST: I have to say I`m relieved. I thought I just wasn`t invited by you. GARTEN: Trust me, nobody`s bored at your house. GUTHRIE: Yes.
