story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:00:16] SAVANNAH GUTHRIE, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Good Thursday morning from Washington and New York. Our top story, all eyes once again on Ukraine. HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Tension there building after new attacks and new threats. It is October 20th. This is Today. Leave immediately, this morning, thousands of residents in southern Ukraine being forced to flee their own homes. Mass evacuations underway after a warning of imminent attacks and martial law declared by Vladimir Putin . And this morning, mounting concern over power outages ahead of a harsh winter, we`ll have the very latest and a live report straight ahead. On the road, President Biden hits the campaign trail today in the closely watched battleground of Pennsylvania. Can he move the needle for the undecided voters with less than three weeks to go? Feeling the freeze, another day of bitter cold across much of the country, parts of the south waking up two record lows, but Al says, hang in there, a big warm ups on the way. They`ll have your full forecast. Consumer alert, the new warning from police after a string of robberies in cities across the country tied to popular online marketplaces. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) CMDR. RODNEY G. HILL, CHICAGO POLICE DEPARTMENT ENGLEWOOD DISTRICT: Nine times out of 10, if you see a deal that is too good to be true, it is. (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB: This morning what you need to know before you click. Those stories, plus, "The Crown" and the controversy. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED MALE: It is with regret, the Prince and Princess of Wales are separating. (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB: The growing backlash against the hit show`s upcoming storyline. Why an Oscar winner wants it to come with a disclaimer and how "The Crown`s" creator is responding. And smash hit. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED MALE: At the wall looking up, see you later. (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB: The Astros defeat the Yankees in game one of the ALCS while the Padres rally to tie up their series with the Phillies in a game for the record books. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) UNIDENTIFIED MALE: Aaron Nola against Austin Nola, little brother against big brother. (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB: The battle of the brothers going down in history, today, Thursday, October 20th, 2022. UNIDENTIFIED MALE: From NBC News, this is Today with Savannah Guthrie live from Washington, D.C. and Hoda Kotb live from Studio 1A in Rockefeller Plaza. KOTB: Well good morning. Good to see you. So happy you`re joining us on a Thursday morning. Savannah is joining us in D.C. And SG, can you imagine being the mom and dad you`re like, I`m cheering for both my sons. You go, no you go. It`s got to be a tough one. GUTHRIE: I know. Yes, moms are always like, no, I don`t have a favorite. No really, I don`t. Well, a lot more of those highlights in just a bit. Plus nearly two thirds of the country waking up to another morning of bitter cold, I know you`re feeling it there in New York, here Washington too. Record low temps expected in the south today. Al is tracking it and he has some good news on when it`ll feel a little more like fall. KOTB: But we are going to start this morning in Ukraine where new evacuations are being ordered. It comes as residents are being told to charge their devices after drone strikes knocked out key power stations, rolling blackouts now common. And this is just as the brutal Ukraine winter is approaching. NBC`s Cal Perry is in Ukraine for us. Cal, good morning. Give us the latest. CAL PERRY, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Hey, good morning to you, Hoda. Fresh strikes overnight, the target once again that vital energy infrastructure of Ukraine. It is what has prompted the mayor here to tell people turn off your electricity, save power. All the while as you mentioned, the bitter cold from the winter has arrived, the temperatures plunging overnight, all the while the strikes continue across Ukrainian cities. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) PERRY (voice-over): This morning, the people of Kherson are caught in the middle. Thousands in the port city that has been under Russian occupation for months, now being ordered to evacuate by Russian installed leaders. Some getting text messages that read, dear residents, evacuate immediately. There will be shelling of residential areas by the armed forces of Ukraine. The evacuations and apparent reaction to Ukraine`s counter offensive in the region, recapturing villages and farmland in recent weeks, Ukrainian officials accusing Russia of trying to create hysteria. It comes on the same day Russian`s President Putin declared martial law in the four Ukrainian regions currently occupied by Russia. I have signed a decree, he said, introducing martial law into these four entities of the Russian Federation. Under the order Russia can, it says, legally seize Ukrainian homes and property, move civilian populations and create local militias, meaning Moscow may try to force Ukrainians to fight against their own country. JOE BIDEN, PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES: It seems his only tool available to him is to brutalize individual citizens in Ukraine. PERRY (voice-over): From Mykolaiv and the south to Kyiv and the north, the Russian bombardment continues. In just over a month, at least 239 drones have been shot down by air defenses, according to the Ukrainian military. The ones that make it past those air defenses are frequently striking infrastructure targets, 30 percent of power plants have been destroyed. [07:05:17] Other times, civilians pay the price. Here in the capital of Kyiv, eight dead in 24 hours, all the while the threat of a nuclear attack looms. Children drill in a nearby school here in Kyiv. And while bulletproof vests are necessary on the battle front, swim caps and goggles must do here on the home front. (END VIDEOTAPE) PERRY: Now Ukraine is asking countries around the world to help with its air defense system. Israel the latest to offer hands saying it will help provide that very important early alert system. But holding back on the ammunition needed to actually shoot down the drones. Officials here are hoping to get that from the United States. Hoda? KOTB: We`re counting those young kids with swim caps and goggles, it`s just -- it`s also unsettling. Thank you so much. We appreciate your report there. Let`s move on back here at home. We`ve got another morning of cold temperatures and a lot of the country, record setting in parts of the South. Let`s bring in Mr. Roker to get a first check of the forecast. Good morning, Al. AL ROKER, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: All right, good morning, Hoda. Good morning, everybody. The good news is if you are one of the 76 million people under these frost advisory, freeze warnings, we`ve got some relief coming for you, so hold on. For this morning though, Memphis 39 degrees, Tallahassee right now 32, Orlando 55 degrees, Norfolk 39. But we are going to see a little bit of a change. For today though, it is going to stay cold but we are going to see a little relief. But for today, about 12 degrees below average in Buffalo behind where the Jetstream dips to the south. We`re looking at Pier 75 degrees, that`s 15 degrees above normal, Boise, Idaho 77. For tomorrow, those temperatures still a little on the chilly side from New York, Charlotte on into Jacksonville. But the warmth is coming, Little Rock 81, San Antonio 86, Dallas, it`s going to be 88 degrees. And as we get into early next week, temperatures moderate, look at this, we`ll be in the 60s in New York right on into early next week, 70s in Raleigh and in Cincinnati, Chicago as well. And hot springs Arkansas into the 80s. We have that record warmth out west, record cold in the east. However, it`s because of this jet stream that`s really been amplified. The good news is if you`re here in the east, we`re going to see a flip, cooler air with rain and snow, which is good news for Seattle and Portland. They have right now the worst air quality in the world because of all the heat and the wildfires. They`re going to see temperatures drop 10 to 25 degrees below normal here in the East, much warmer as we get into next week with temperatures 10 to 20 degrees above normal. So Savannah, we`re all getting some good news back to you. GUTHRIE: All right, I like that Al. Thank you. Well, this morning, new data is out. And it reveals more about the effects of inflation on families all across this country, and the Federal Reserve`s efforts to get it under control. This is some top business leaders are voicing big concerns about the months ahead. NBC`s Tom Costello here with us in Washington tracking it again. Not good news that we`re hearing from business leaders. TOM COSTELLO, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Not good news. And we`ve been talking for months about persistent sky high inflation. And now, the head of one of the country`s biggest banks, Goldman Sachs is warning about a possible volatile period as we head into 2023. Listen, when Goldman talks, people listen, for the average family, there`s less concern right now about whether we are entering a recession or already there, but rather, when will things improve and how do we cope right now. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) COSTELLO (voice-over): From Main Street, USA to Wall Street, Americans are still staring down red hot inflation that shows no signs of cooling off. Now some top executives are warning of potentially tough times in the months ahead. DAVID SOLOMON , GOLDMAN SACHS CEO: I think it`s a time to be cautious. That doesn`t mean for sure that we have a really difficult economic scenario. But in the distribution of outcomes, there`s good chance we could have a recession. COSTELLO (voice-over): And Amazon founder, Jeff Bezos , also issuing a warning earlier this week tweeting, the probabilities in this economy tell you to batten down the hatches. With less than three weeks before the midterm elections, President Biden denies that the move to continue tapping into the nation`s emergency oil supply is politically motivated, calling on oil companies to increase production and their refining operations. BIDEN: You still make a significant profit. Your shareholders will still do very well. And the American people catch a break they deserve and get a fair price at the pump as well. COSTELLO (voice-over): But gas is just one part of the global inflation picture. In the U.K. inflation is running even hotter, above 10 percent. Food up a staggering 14.6 percent while the average American family now spends nearly $450 more per month to buy the same goods as last year. The head of the country`s largest retailer, Walmart , tell Savannah it`s hitting people in different ways. [07:10:00] GUTHRIE: Do you feel like consumers are hitting that point where they`re done paying those high prices? JOHN FURNER , WALMART U.S. CEO: I think it depends on the personal situation that consumers are in, really different depending on where you are around the country. COSTELLO (voice-over): For Stephanie Lane`s (ph) family of six living off a single income in Pennsylvania, it`s meant cutting back across the board. STEPHANIE LANE (ph), PENNSYLVANIA RESIDENT: It`s a hard pill to swallow when you have to really change everything you`ve done. And do it everything differently because you can`t afford it. COSTELLO (voice-over): Despite the challenging times, Stephanie (ph) says she and her family are looking forward. LANE (ph): We don`t know when it`s going to get better. But I do know it will. I have faith that it will. (END VIDEOTAPE) GUTHRIE: Tom, we`ve been talking so much about the Fed`s interest rates hikes and how it`s going into effect. And sometimes it takes time to see if they`re working. We`re already seeing some leading indicators right now turning up and affect in the economy. COSTELLO: Last week, you and I talked about a lagging indicator. The unemployment rate is a lagging indicator of what the economy is like right now. We have a new leading indicator, this is concerning. New home building fell 8 percent last month, the lowest since the earliest days of the pandemic, that`s a concern. Mortgage rates, of course, now up to 7.2 percent on a 30 year, that`s double in a year. As a result, existing home sales, we expect are going to be sliding dramatically when we get that data in and price is expected to fall dramatically. All of that is not good for the economy. GUTHRIE: All right, Tom, thank you so much. And, of course, another big focus here in Washington, the midterm elections, which is 19 days to go. Early voting already underway, President Biden is hitting the campaign trail in the battleground of Pennsylvania today. And that brings us over here to Kristen Welker, who`s been covering politics, of course. Well, let`s start here with gas prices. We talked to Tom about the economy, gas prices, is a leading indicator, both economically and politically for the White House. KRISTEN WELKER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: That`s absolutely right. And there`s no doubt that there`s a lot of concern about gas prices, which have ticked up a bit over the past month. They`re down significantly, though, from their high in the summer over $5 a gallon. Yesterday, President Biden announced they`re releasing another 15 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. But look, this is really the tail end of an announcement that was made several months ago to release 180 million barrels. And Savannah, it`s not clear it`s going to have a big impact on gas prices. What it does is it allows the President to make the case that he is working on this issue, which 44 percent of Americans say is their top issue right now heading into these midterms. I talked to the White House Chief of Staff Ron Klain , what`s the first thing he does every morning? Check gas prices. And it underscores, Savannah, the fact that what happens in November could very much be determined by the price of the pump. GUTHRIE: Yes, because it`s something that absolutely everyone feels and it creates a ripple through the economy. Let`s talk about the issue of abortion. Democrats thought they had a lot of momentum with that issue right on the heels of the Dobbs decision in June. Now, it doesn`t seem that it`s having as much of a sway with independent voters. WELKER: That`s right. And you look at the swing that we`re seeing among independent women in particular, who said that they favored Democrats in September. Now, huge swing over to Republicans, you saw abortion as an energizing factor in races in Kansas in special election in New York in the primaries, but I think Democrats are concerned that they need to be having a broader appeal. You saw President Biden talking about the issue of abortion earlier this week. He said remember, basically the outrage that you felt on the day that Roe v. Wade was overturned, trying to turn back the clock in essence, Savannah, but there`s a real awareness and I think a message from the White House. Yes, we need to talk about abortion. But we need to talk about issues including the economy and crime that voters care about in this election cycle, too. So that`s why the President is going to be in Pennsylvania talking about infrastructure today, for example. GUTHRIE: Yes, the polls have shown that the Republicans appeared to have some momentum going into these midterms. The control of the Senate, control of the House is on the table, Pennsylvania, where the President will be today is a key Senate race and it`s tight. WELKER: It`s very tight. It`s basically a statistical dead heat, Savannah. And what`s notable about the President stop in Pennsylvania today, he`s going to be talking about infrastructure. And here you can see these polls between John Fetterman and Dr. Oz. He`s going to talk about infrastructure and then hold a fundraising event with John Fetterman . So not the typical rally that you would usually see a President hold in these closing weeks of a campaign. Why? Well, his approval ratings are low. And I think a lot of Democrats are concerned that he will hurt, he will hinder them instead of helping them. And so that`s why I think you`re not seeing these traditional rallies. But I spoke to an administration official who said, look, the bottom line is, we think it`s more effective to have him out talking about things like infrastructure, talking about things like abortion, gas prices, the things that he has worked on, instead of basically shouting at a crowd. They point to Obama, they point to Trump, they say, look, they had big losses in their midterms as well. So they don`t necessarily see that as an effective strategy. They`re also saying he will be holding typical events getting closer. GUTHRIE: All right, Kristen Welker here in Washington with me. Thank you so much. Hoda to 14 minutes after the hour, I`ll send it over to you. [07:15:01] KOTB: All right, thank you SG. story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:00:16] SAVANNAH GUTHRIE, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Good morning. It`s Tuesday. Hope you have those winter coats handy. NBC`s chief foreign correspondent Richard Engel has the very latest. Hey, Richard, good morning. RICHARD ENGEL, NBC NEWS CHIEF FOREIGN CORRESPONDENT: Good morning, Hoda. Russia is now attacking Ukrainian cities daily and with impunity. This was the main flower market here in the city of Mykolaiv was hit by a Russian missile overnight. And just down the street, Russia attacked an apartment building killing at least one person according to Ukrainian officials. For Irina Shipchenko (ph), whose flower shop was destroyed overnight in Mykolaiv, what Russia is doing is nothing less than state terror. We clean up and continue living. What else can we do and we will win, she says. Over the last two weeks, Russia has intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities, claiming to be destroying the country`s infrastructure and its ability to wage war. But Russia is firing directly on civilians attacking an apartment building overnight in Mykolaiv, too. Officials say Russia launched a guided missile, killing one person. The strikes came hours after an airplane mysteriously crashed in Russia. State media reporting that a pilot on a training mission took off from an occupied part of Ukraine and ejected, the aircraft smashing into a building and killing four Russians. Ukrainians wonder if it was an accident or sabotage from within. President Putin personally dispatched investigators to the scene. Discontent is growing in Russia after the Kremlin imposed the draft, rounding up conscripts across the country. And with precision weapons in short supply, Moscow is increasingly relying on Iranian made dive bomber drones, launching them in swarms at Ukrainian cities including Kyiv with deadly effect. Overnight in his daily address, President Zelenskyy called for more air defenses. Secretary of State Blinken condemned Iran for supplying Russia with weapons. The United States gives Ukraine billions of dollars in military support, but not long range weapons, trying to find a perhaps impossible balance of supporting Ukraine without antagonizing Moscow excessively. In a sign, both sides seemed to recognize this will be a long war. Russia and Ukraine exchanged prisoners 108 Ukrainian women for captured Russian soldiers in a one to one swap. (END VIDEOTAPE) ENGEL: Over the last several days, we`ve been talking a lot about how Russia is using those Iranian made drones. The drones are highly effective. Elnaz Rekabi competed on Sunday with what appeared to be a headband her hair uncovered which is a violation of Iran strict dress code. Now this morning, an apology on her Instagram page, but there`s still growing concern for her safety. Elnaz Rekabi, a prominent rock climber, took part in a competition in South Korea this weekend, notably climbing with her head uncovered. In the past, Rekabi has worn the traditional headscarf while climbing. The hijab has been a focus of recent extraordinary protests in Iran, sparked by the death of 22-year- old Mahsa Amini who was detained by the morality police for breaching the dress code. She died three days later. Women across Iran have protested by cutting their hair and appearing in public with their heads uncovered. After the appearance in South Korea, Rekabi is headed home. The Iranian embassy in Seoul tweeting she departed yesterday. Human rights groups have been concerned about pressure she may face from authorities. MAHMOOD AMIRY-MOGHADDAM, DIRECTOR OF NGO IRAN HUMAN RIGHTS: I think they will put her under tremendous pressure. There is fear of torture, ill treatment, psychological pressure. They want to set an example both for other athletes in the same situation and also for the Iranian girls so that they don`t get a role model in Elnaz. FITZGERALD (voice-over): Rekabi this morning posting on Instagram that her job had issues before she was called to climb. While the statement was posted on her account, the circumstances under which he was posted remain unclear. Now back in Iran, the regime has been under pressure as protests led by young women continue, many watching Rekabi`s returned to the country with concern. (END VIDEOTAPE) FITZGERALD: Now the International Federation of sports climbing says it`s in contact with Rekabi. They also say they`re in contact with the Iranian Climbing Federation. And we turn now to the midterms with just three weeks to go early in person voting is now underway across a number of stakes. And at stake, control of the Senate and the House. And let`s start right there with the issues that voters say matter to them. And what that`s telling us about what might happen here and these elections. And it does seem that as the economy moved to center stage, Republicans are improving their chances here. GUTHRIE: And a few weeks ago, it was the Democrats who had the advantage there. So you see the momentum in these final weeks. Let`s talk about the issue of crime, not high on the list of voters concerns and yet it seems to be making an impact in certain races. KORNACKI: It`s fascinating because we showed you the top issue voters have, crime doesn`t rate high there, doesn`t mean it`s not on their mind. So let`s show you a place where I think it is having an impact. This is Wisconsin, one of the key Senate races, Ron Johnson to term Republican incumbent. He leads in the polling average over his Democratic challenger. Now Johnson has been leaning heavily on crime. [07:15:00] Interesting poll that came out of Wisconsin this week they asked things a little bit differently. They basically asked, are these issues important to you? That`s what`s being asked here. Inflation tops the list. But look at crime. It`s close to 90 percent. And I think also striking, abortion is under 80 percent. Republicans running heavily on crime, Democrats running heavily on abortion, and it looks like in this Wisconsin race, crime may have more resonance than abortion does. GUTHRIE: Making a big difference in Pennsylvania Senate race as well, it appears. But let`s talk about Georgia, because it may just be Georgia, Georgia, Georgia to quote our friend Tim Russert. That might be the decision maker in terms of who controls Congress. KORNACKI: Yes, I mean, again, we saw this two years ago, Georgia is a runoff state. If nobody gets 50 percent and here`s that Senate race, Raphael Warnock , Herschel Walker , Warnock leading but nobody had 50. If nobody cracks 50, it`s a December 6th runoff, could have control of the Senate on the line. They did have a debate last Friday. We`re waiting to get a readout from some polls haven`t really seen it yet if that change anything there. GUTHRIE: Real quickly, the governor`s race is interesting because it doesn`t look like people are at least telling pollsters they`re going to vote straight down party lines. KORNACKI: We thought this type of voter was extinct, the split ticket voter. But look in Georgia, Brian Kemp , the Republican governor, pretty comfortably ahead outperforming the other Republican, Herschel Walker . What pollsters say they`re seeing here is there`s a suburban voter outside Atlanta who doesn`t like Biden, doesn`t like the Democrats but also doesn`t like Donald Trump . And, you know, Brian Kemp went to political war with Donald Trump and he survived in that voters eyes. Kemp`s OK. Walker`s got some convincing to do. story_text: (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [07:00:16] SAVANNAH GUTHRIE, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Good morning. It`s Tuesday. Hope you have those winter coats handy. HODA KOTB, NBC NEWS ANCHOR: Yes, and in several cities, they`re already breaking out the snow shovels. It is October 18th. And this is Today. Deep freeze, nearly 100 million people waking up to brutally cold temperatures from Colorado to New England all the way down to Florida, some places in between coping with the earliest snowfall in years. It`s going to be a long winter. We are alive where the flakes are falling and Al will have your full forecast. Breaking overnight, cities across Ukraine facing a new barrage of Russian airstrikes, this time, cutting power and water supplies to tens of thousands of civilians, the very latest in a live report from the front lines. Growing concern, an Iranian athlete in the international spotlight after competing in a high profile event without her hijab, so was it a show of support for women protesting on the streets back home, her new message overnight and what she`s facing as she returns to Tehran. Three weeks to go, with the midterms fast approaching candidates from coast to coast clashing in closely watched debates overnight, just ahead, we will break down the key races where they stand and the biggest issues on the minds of voters. headline: Conversation With Elizabeth Heiskell About Her Breast Cancer Journey
story_text: HODA KOTB: We are back. 8:13. The "Pink Power TODAY". And this morning story hits close to home for us. SAVANNAH GUTHRIE: Yes, our beloved "TODAY" food contributor Elizabeth Heiskell was diagnosed with stage two breast cancer this past summer. KOTB: Like a lot of women this can happen, too. She was in the best shape of her life. She has no family history. She says breast cancer wasn`t just -- well, not on her radar. Elizabeth, we love you. You are here with us. ELIZABETH HEISKELL, " TODAY" FOOD CONTRIBUTOR: Yes. KOTB: We are going to talk to you in a second. OK. But first, let`s check out her story. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) HEISKELL: I was diagnosed with stage two breast cancer. KOTB (voiceover): Elizabeth found a lump by chance. HEISKELL: I went to just scratch my chest and I found a lump. I thought that I had had a mammogram eight months ago. I wasn`t that concerned, honestly. KOTB (voiceover): But she had the lump checked by her doctor. HEISKELL: She felt around and she started to look very panicked. We got to get a mammogram. We got to get an ultrasound. We need to get a biopsy. KOTB (voiceover): Elizabeth thought she was up to date with her mammogram screenings but the doctor informed her otherwise. HEISKELL: She said, Elizabeth it`s been two years, almost two and a half years since you had it. KOTB (voiceover): The news she had breast cancer came as a complete shock. It was like the wind had been knocked out of me, like somebody punched me. I was not prepared for this. I was in the best shape of my life. I had just lost a good amount of weight. Breast cancer was not on my radar at all. It took me to my knees. [08:15:00] I have no family history of breast cancer. That was another reason I was so blindsided by this. As hard as it is for somebody to tell you that you have cancer, as hard as that is to hear, it is impossible to say the words to your family. Honestly, I didn`t think I was going to be able to process it to say that sentence to my family. It took weeks and weeks for it to even sink in. I just finished my third chemo treatment. I am just now grasping the fact that I have cancer. KOTB (voiceover): Cooking brought some comfort. HEISKELL: I must have made meat loaf, mashed potatoes, and sort of green peas with cream sauce. This was what -- what my mother made for me. I don`t even know how many times I made that meal because it did, it brought me such comfort. I was diagnosed three weeks before mama passed away. So, it`s been a lot. We are going to do these great easy salads that we can -- KOTB (voiceover): As a well-known chef and "TODAY" contributor, Elizabeth says she is passionate about cooking and taking care of others, but cancer has forced her to focus on herself. HEISKELL: It`s not my nature. I bring the casseroles. I bring the food. I am the doer. I am the one that makes sure that everyone else is OK. And it`s easy to let that take over and you forget to take care of yourself. You just have to take it step by step, day by day. But you will, you will get there. You will get to the top of the mountain. (END VIDEO CLIP) KOTB (on camera): Yes, you will. Yes, you will, Elizabeth. GUTHRIE: yes. KOTB: We are so happy that you are sitting here on this couch. We want to know all about it. But just in this moment, like, how are you -- tell me the prognosis. How are you feeling today? HEISKELL: You know, I am so unbelievably grateful. So, we went back to MD Anderson and that little tumor has shrunk 78 percent. GUTHRIE: Wow. Wow. Wow. KOTB: Come on. HEISKELL: That was only -- that was after three chemo treatments. KOTB: Wow. HEISKELL: I mean, it`s unbelievable. And I`m just -- I am -- I`m so grateful that I`m almost -- I feel guilty at times, you know, because I have the most amazing support system. I have you all. I have family and friends. And, you know, an incredible health care. And, you know, it`s good. It`s good. GUTHRIE: So, you`re halfway through your chemo. You`ll have your surgery. But -- I mean, to have that kind of, it`s working? HEISKELL: Yes. GUTHRIE: The feeling must be such, such a -- you know, just an inspiration? HEISKELL: It was unbelievable. And the lady that did my ultrasound, she -- her -- my mother`s name was Sheila (ph). Her name was Sheila (ph). She spelled it just like my mother did. And then her daughter`s name was Elizabeth and we have the same birthday. GUTHRIE: Oh, my gosh. HEISKELL: So, if you don`t tell me that my mama wasn`t all up in that room. GUTHRIE: Oh, wow. HEISKELL: But you know, the thing is, is that this is -- it is a journey. You know, it is a climb. And I`m leaning in and I`m learning. You know, I`m learning so much. And, you know, it`s -- I had worked myself up. When I was getting ready for that first chemo treatment, honey, fear had taken over. It was driving the bus. You would have thought that I was going to go in there and they were taking off all my fingers, all my toes. Like, I was petrified. KOTB: Yes. HEISKELL: And so, I got through that day and Luke was with me and I literally -- everything they did, I said, oh, that wasn`t so bad. KOTB: Yes. HEISKELL: Well, I mean, that wasn`t so bad. So, by the time I got home, I called my girls and I said, look -- I said, fear is not going to drive this bus. It -- to dream, it`s -- you use the same exact brain, the same exact creativity to make those horrible nightmares as you do to dream. And I am not doing it any more. KOTB: That`s it. HEISKELL: I am not holding back. You all think that I`ve always been 100 percent. There is something that I have been holding back and I`m not going to do it anymore. I am not fearing. KOTB: You said there are things that cancer could -- is teaching you that nothing else could have taught you. Because everyone knows that adage of God only gives you as much as you can handle. HEISKELL: Yes. KOTB: You actually don`t believe that? HEISKELL: No, I don`t think that`s the case. I think it`s time for you to lean in and learn something new. And, you know, the lessons that I have learned -- I mean, it`s look for silver linings even in this mess. There was this sweetest lady when I was at the clinic. And, you know, they give us these warm robes. So, it -- kind of, for five minutes you feel like you are at a spa, until they take your boob and they stick it into a vice grip. For that minute, you know -- and so, as she looked at me and she is sitting there with her bald head and sunken eyes, and she said, oh -- she said, aren`t these robes just the silver lining? And I had just been diagnosed, and I thought silver lining my butt. We are sitting here, you know. And then it came to me. And then she said, you know, where you live? And I said, I live in Oxford. She said, bus -- but my sister-in-law lives here in Houston so I have a place to stay. She goes, another silver lining. And it was almost like she was catching butterflies. I am not kidding you. And so, if you stay there in that silver lining, that silver lining is going to be the thing that you`re going to wrap yourself in. That`s all you`re going to see is the silver. And I`m telling you, these are the lessons that I would have -- I mean, and I know we talk about it and we say, you know. But to really believe -- KOTB: Believe it. GUTHRIE: Yes. HEISKELL: -- and every day you are looking for the silver lining butterflies. [08:20:00] KOTB: One of your silver linings is standing over there. You talked about your tribe. HEISKELL: Yes. KOTB: Your people. Who do we have? HEISKELL: So, I have my daddy, who I love more than life itself. And it`s his birthday tomorrow. And then I have Mindy and my sweet husband, Luke who -- let me tell you something, Luke looked at me in my first cancer treatment. And he looked over and I was sitting there and he had tears in his eyes when they went to put the first chemo drug in my body. And he looked at me and I know he was thinking, if only I could just take this and put this in me right now. He has been everything. You cannot even imagine. And my girls. Oh, my gosh, and my friends. KOTB: Is that one of your brothers? HEISKELL: And my friends -- no. And that`s Molly. And we have Margie (ph) and Peter. And -- you know, I do. I have a whole tribe. I have a little boy that every day when he goes to school, he tells his dad to honk the horn and -- so that I know that they are praying for me that morning. I mean, there is -- you cannot imagine. I have somebody who sent me a night light because I`d said that when the fear was taking -- driving the bus, I was up late nights. I mean, it was tough. And so, she sent me a night light that I could turn on when I was up scared at night. I mean, these are the people that I have. And, you know, I hope that people that, if you know somebody that has breast cancer or cancer or that`s struggling, please go out of your way. It doesn`t have to be much. KOTB: Right. HEISKELL: A honk of the horn or a night light, anything. KOTB: And sometimes people think, well, you know what, they may want their family time. They may want their privacy. But reach out, right? HEISKELL: Lean into them. KOTB: Lean in, yes. HEISKELL: Get under them. KOTB: Yes. HEISKELL: Hold them up. KOTB: Hold them. HEISKELL: And carry them up that mountain. I mean -- KOTB: Yes. GUTHRIE: Call, don`t text. KOTB: Yes. HEISKELL: Yes. And they did call me. You all they called me. KOTB: Of course. HEISKELL: And of course, when I was driving back from Memphis, we had been to the oncologist when you called, and I was like, oh God. Lord. Look, Hoda`s on the phone. Stop the car. Because we were about to go through a dead area. I was like, Hoda never calls me. Just stop the car. And then Savannah called. And it was just amazing. KOTB: Well, we -- GUTHRIE: We love you. KOTB: You`re our family. GUTHRIE: You are our family. KOTB: We`re part of your tribe, too. HEISKELL: Well, that -- I have been looking forward to being back here with you all so much. And you are -- I mean, I am. I`m back with family. I`m with Debbie and my producer, who I -- who really, I mean, she is my family. KOTB: Well, we adore you. You need to -- all of this is, like, the most inspirational. GUTHRIE: I know. It really is. KOTB: I`m sure you helped a ton of people today. We love you. HEISKELL: Go get your mammograms. KOTB: Yes. HEISKELL: I literally thought it was eight months. It had been two years people. KOTB: Yes. GUTHRIE: Yes. HEISKELL: It had been two years people. KOTB: You got it. HEISKELL: You put it on your calendar right now. You stop what you`re doing. I`m serious. KOTB: Yes. GUTHRIE: Yes, absolutely. KOTB: We love you. We love you. GUTHRIE: We love you. headline: The World-Famous Hollywood Sign Gets A Touch Up Just In Time For A Huge Anniversary
story_text: KRISTEN WELKER: Well, if you`ve ever traveled to Los Angeles, you`ve probably looked high on the Hill to see that world famous Hollywood sign. PETER ALEXANDER: You almost don`t have to travel to Los Angeles to have seen that sign. WELKER: That is right, everywhere. ALEXANDER: It`s like ubiquitous. A big anniversary is approaching for the sign and now it`s getting a pretty nice touch up. NBC`s Steve Patterson grabbed a paintbrush and got to work. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) STEVE PATTERSON, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT (voice over): Every great city has a symbol, representing the ideals of its people. In Hollywood, it`s a sign. Nine giant letters spelling out one iconic notion. This is where dreams are made. Believe it or not, the Hollywood sign is about to turn 100 years old, it was meant to last just 18 months. The sign went up back in 1923 as Hollywoodland, a billboard to sell real estate, but it caught people`s attention and stuck around. In the 40s, it was donated to the city of Los Angeles and the land was removed. JEFF ZARRINNAM, HOLLYWOOD SIGN TRUST CHAIR: The sign came to mean something different. It came to mean the Hollywood industry as a whole. PATTERSON: Through the years, the old wooden sign decayed, even losing one of its O`s. So, in 1978, the old one was knocked down and a new wood rose in its place. Now, it`s getting a fresh coat of paint ahead of its big birthday. ROGER MARTINEZ, DUGGAN AND ASSOCIATES SUPERINTENDENT: It honestly feels like you know, you`re kind of like one of the stars up here. All right, let`s go. PATTERSON: Roger Martinez, he`s overseeing the repainting process. He took me up to lend a hand. MARTINEZ: Ready to help with paint? PATTERSON: I`m ready. MARTINEZ: Use the roller yourself. PATTERSON: I would never dream that I would be putting paint on the Hollywood sign. MARTINEZ: Dreams come true. PATTERSON: Dreams do come true. MARTINEZ: Remember, this is Hollywood. PATTERSON: This is Hollywood, this is where it happens, right? MARTINEZ: I`m the guardian of the Hollywood sign. PATTERSON: Jeff Zarrinnam runs the Hollywood sign trust. ZARRINNAM: People have grown accustomed to seeing the sign. But it also has a meaning in their hearts. And they relate to the sign to their favorite actor, their television show, their movie, and that`s what it means to people around the world. PATTERSON: In a place where dreams of stardom are made and dashed, the message high up here endures. A symbol of the stars shining down on Tinseltown for generations to come. [07:50:10] For TODAY, Steve Patterson, NBC News, Hollywood. (END VIDEO CLIP) WELKER: Talk about dreams coming true. So cool Steve got to help paint. WALKER: And I`ll be a senator that protects life. And I say that was a lie. And I`m not backing down. BARBER (voice-over): Throughout the debate, Warnock tried to emphasize his work in Washington. WARNOCK: I passed the single largest tax cut, contrary to what my opponent is suggesting for middle and working class families in American history. BARBER (voice-over): And paint Walker as unqualified. WARNOCK: I`ve never pretended to be a police officer. And I`ve never, I`ve never threatened a shootout with the police. UNDENTIFIED FEMALE: That is not allowed, sir. I asked you to put that prop away. BARBER (voice-over): Walker tried to focus on the economy. WALKER: You have to blame this administration and Senator Warnock, because within two years, this inflation has gotten worse. BARBER (voice-over): And tie Warnock to a president whose approval rating among Georgia voters is 37 percent. WALKER: Can you tell me why he voted me Joe Biden 96 percent of the time if you`ve seen it for Georgia? BARBER (voice-over): Every topic Georgia voters have the final word and early voting begins Monday and race that could determine which party controls the United States Senate . (END VIDEOTAPE) BARBER: And Georgia and ordered to avoid a runoff a candidate has to pass a 50 percent threshold and recent polling. These candidates are in a statistical tie. All that plus there`s no Hogwarts without Hagrid. ROBBIE COLTRANE, SPANISH ACTOR: Rubeus Hagrid, keeper of keys engravings at Hogwarts. Robbie Coltrane is going to be missed. WELKER: He sure is. Those who knew him described him as boisterous and eccentric. And we will look back at his life at his legacy. Yes. Meantime, the Republican Senate candidate in Georgia backed by President Trump, Herschel Walker , appeared on stage with incumbent Democratic candidate Raphael Warnock for their only debate overnight. ALEXANDER: Georgia is one of at least three crucial battleground states with very high-stakes Senate races at stake there. They could determine whether the Democrats retain control or if the Republicans will take it away. So we want to begin this morning with NBC`s Ellison Barber. She`s in Savannah with a wrap-up of last night`s big showdown, Ellison, good morning. ELLISON BARBER, NBC NEWS CORRESPONDENT: Good morning, Peter. This is a closely watched race. This debate was highly anticipated. This morning, both campaigns are declaring victory. headline: Behind The Scenes Of Carrie Underwood`s Epic New Tour
story_text: SHEINELLE JONES: I am excited for this. So, this morning, we have a "TODAY" exclusive. A first look at what to expect when country superstar Carrie Underwood hits the road for her Denim and Rhinestones tour. It`s her first in three years since she took me back stage in South Carolina where it all kicks off. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) CARRIE UNDERWOOD, SINGER: It`s a good time. A lot of hard work has gone into the show and very, very proud of it. People are going to have fun. JONES (voiceover): It`s been a few years since a Carrie Underwood tour has made its way across the country. And no one seems more excited than the superstar herself.\\ JONES (on camera): What is the one thing you miss about touring? UNDERWOOD: The crowds. I love to sing. When I`m on stage, I feel like I am at home. And just to feel the energy from people and you look out at all these seats and every single person that is there. JONES (voiceover): The eight-time Grammy winner embarking on a 43-stop arena tour, kicking it all off with a huge show in Greenville, South Carolina. And yours truly is given an all-access pass. JONES (on camera): This gives me like the feels. UNDERWOOD: It`s pretty awesome. It looks bigger. I feel like from up here. JONES: From here? UNDERWOOD: Yes. JONES (voiceover): The stage for her "Denim and Rhinestones" tour lit in dramatic purple will include pyrotechnics and even Carrie performing some high-flying aerial stunts. UNDERWOOD: I am always looking to do things I`ve never have done before. JONES (on camera): Like fly? UNDERWOOD: Like fly. JONES (voiceover): Carrie, taking a page out of her CMT Awards performance. UNDERWOOD: And it`s important to me to make sure like everybody gets a good view. So, we want to figure out some cool ways to get from point A to point B. JONES (on camera): How exciting is that? JONES (voiceover): It`s all part of her goal to bring something new to the arena tours. UNDERWOOD: I want everything to feel different. I don`t want somebody to be like, no, I saw a Carrie Underwood show, you know, four years ago and I`m good. JONES (voiceover): Something definitely worth the price of admission, Carrie`s stunning wardrobe. JONES (on camera): Like this is -- UNDERWOOD: It`s a lot. There`s a lot going. JONES: It`s amazing. Look how beautiful it is. UNDERWOOD: The last part is adding more rhinestones. JONES: I don`t know if you could add any more rhinestones. UNDERWOOD: You always can. I mean -- JONES (voiceover): But something no amount of rhinestones can replace, Carrie`s time with her kids on the tour and at home. [09:35:00] UNDERWOOD: They will be out to visit. This tour, I`m going home a lot more than I ever have before. There is a way to get me home even if it`s just for the day. JONES (on camera): So, are your kids aware of what mommy does? I mean, they`ve been on tour with you before but they are young. UNDERWOOD: I feel like Israel who is seven and a half, he is becoming more aware that it`s not normal, probably because of people around him. So, he`ll go to school and somebody will be, like, I saw your mom on TV last night. JONES (voiceover): One of the Carrie`s few must-haves, a mobile gym. JONES (on camera): This is good. Do you ever work out to your own music? UNDERWOOD: No. JONES: No. UNDERWOOD: It`s weird. JONES (voiceover): A U.S. arena tour, a long way from Carrie`s "American Idol" days. JONES (on camera): Let me take you back. UNDERWOOD: Yes. JONES: It was in 2005. I was a reporter in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and I had the assignment to meet you at the door. The whole town was going nuts because a local girl made it on "American idol." And you walked in and your hands were like -- and I grabbed your hand. I was like, are you ready? If you look at this picture, like this girl right here, do you remember what you were feeling in those early days? UNDERWOOD: At that point, it was all very new, very fresh. And I am, like, OK, you know, let`s enjoy this and have fun and, you know, keep trying to, you know, move forward, but it could all go away at any second. And I think it`s kind of important to treat everything like that, you know, because it just makes you grateful. So, I still -- I`m waiting for the moment where I`m like feeling like I belong. JONES: Are you kidding me? JONES (voiceover): And while I had her, I just had to ask. (MUSIC PLAYING) JONES (on camera): One of your fellow "American Idol" winners, you know, Kelly Clarkson, does her Kellyoke. Have you heard her sing "Before He Cheats?" UNDERWOOD: I have. I have. I feel like she`s one person that you`re like, please, don`t sing my song because you`re going to make me look bad. JONES: Are you joking? You all are both like powerhouses. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: That`s funny. I was asking her, you know, if she stays in touch with some of the -- you know, the folks who she, you know, was on "Idol" with years ago. And she has -- great. She says she still talks to Simon, you know, that whole thing. DREYER: Oh, that`s great. JONES: One thing I will say about Carrie is she is so humble and it`s not lost on her. Because I`m like, oh, my god, look at all these clothes and look at all of this. And she is like, yes. You know, she just -- it keeps it -- DREYER: It seems like it hasn`t gone to her head. JONES: Not at all. DREYER: She`s walking around like, can you -- JONES: She is still saying, can you believe it? DREYER: Yes. JONES: I know. DREYER: That`s great. JONES: The tour kicks off tomorrow and tickets are on sale now. There will be pyrotechnics. She flies, as we talked about. She even -- she`s like, I am humble and even -- SOBOROFF: I want to see you get up on the flying thing. JONES: I loved it. Yes. ROKER: Oh, yes. DREYER: With that old hairstyle. JONES: Exactly. DREYER: Yes. JONES: Exactly. DREYER: All right. Coming up, another icon is here with us in studio. She`s -- SOBOROFF: There she is. DREYER: Stella McCartney . You`re going to fashion, family and so much more, right? STELLA MCCARTNEY , FASHION DESIGNER: Absolutely. DREYER: OK. When we come back. SOBOROFF: Don`t go anywhere. JONES: Gorgeous. Gorgeous. SOBOROFF: Nice done. Nice walk off. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [09:40:00] JONES: We have our life therapist here. She`s also -- SOBOROFF: Really have a good time JONES: -- a fashion royalty with us this morning here in studio. SOBOROFF: Stella McCartney has made a name for herself designing clothes for celebrities like Meghan Markle , Amal Clooney, Beyonce Johnson, so, so many more. DREYER: She launched her brand in 2001, pioneering animal free and ecofriendly fashion. ROKER: And Stella joining us now fresh off her Paris fashion show. JONES: Yes. ROKER: Good morning, Stella. JONES: Good morning. STELLA MCCARTNEY , FASHION DESIGNER: Hi. SOBOROFF: Good to see you. MCCARTNEY: Good morning. ROKER: So, you made this a part of your mission, you know, sustainable ecofriendly. I mean, Bella Hadid`s Met`s dress in the Paris fashion show you making a big splash. How important is that to you and why did you decide so early on? I mean, you were really ahead of the curve on this. MCCARTNEY: You know, I grew up on an organic farm in England as a vegetarian and I basically wanted to be a fashion designer and I was lucky enough to be one and I thought, I can`t compromise my ethics for my career. I don`t want to kill animals. You know, billions of animals get killed for handbags and shoes and leather jackets. So, I was like, I can`t do that. I need to find an alternative. And it started there really. And, you know, the best thing about today is that actually doing sustainable fashion and being ethical and conscious is actually on trend. JONES: It`s in. SOBOROFF: That`s true. MCCARTNEY: Which is a miracle. JONES: Right. DREYER: Is it hard to do? MCCARTNEY: It`s impossible to do. DREYER: Yes. MCCARTNEY: It`s a miracle that I am here today. It`s really, really hard. You know, you have to work with your suppliers so deeply. But it`s this kind of sexiest thing, I think, in fashion. It`s the future of fashion. I think if people don`t start adopting this way of working, then, you know, they`re going to go out of fashion pretty quick. JONES: Yes. SOBOROFF: Thanks in no small part to everything that you have done. And Al mentioned, by the way, at Paris Fashion Week, I want to ask you about that because saw your dad was there, your sister Mary was your photographer. MCCARTNEY: Yes. SOBOROFF: A real family affair. How was it? You guys have a good time? You guys always go together as a group? MCCARTNEY: No. I mean, I`m always there. But, you know, my dad is a busy guy. So, when he can come, I`m always so excited. And, you know, family, the most important thing, right? Let`s face it. Family and friends. And, you know, the fashion industry is a tough cookie and to have your family there supporting you. You know, my family happened to be fabulous. So, it adds a little diamond. SOBOROFF: Understatement. JONES: That`s fair to say. SOBOROFF: I saw -- speaking of your dad, that he posted -- he is almost 80 and he`s doing -- still doing head stands. Here it is. ROKER: Wow. SOBOROFF: Wait. Guys, look in the corner of the TV screen. He is watching MS and there a teaser for our documentary series. So, shout out -- JONES: Oh, look at that, Jacob. SOBOROFF: Shout out to Mr. McCartney. JONES: So, that`s why you -- MCCARTNEY: There you go. SOBOROFF: Do you do that too? MCCARTNEY: I will be sending a check in the post. SOBOROFF: Yes. Thank you very much. MCCARTNEY: And you are going to owe him a couple of pounds. SOBOROFF: Are you a head stander? MCCARTNEY: Yes, I can do the head stand. SOBOROFF: Really? MCCARTNEY: But my dad is very religious about it. He does eye exercises. You know, I mean, he just headlined Glassenbury (ph) a couple of months ago. JONES: Yes. MCCARTNEY: A week after turning 80 to 250,000 people. So, he must be doing something right. JONES: I love it. MCCARTNEY: Should all we do one now? SOBOROFF: No. No, thank you. JONES: You know what, earlier this year you were awarded -- somebody in my ear goes, yes, please. Are you joking? MCCARTNEY: Yes. JONES: Earlier this year you were awarded the CBE. So, it`s the Commander of the Order of the British Empire by the late Queen Elizabeth. MCCARTNEY: I know. SOBOROFF: Amazing. JONES: For your services to fashion and sustainability. Your father, of course, is knighted. And you also designed the dress that Meghan Markle wore at the queen`s funeral? MCCARTNEY: I did. JONES: What an honor. [09:45:00] MCCARTNEY: Yes. Well, you know, it is a real honor, actually. It`s funny. I don`t know. You know, it`s hard to not kind of pinch yourself when these things happen. And yes, I have another award coming up. I`m really excited. I`m -- ROKER: Do tell. SOBOROFF: Tell us about it. MCCARTNEY: It`s the -- oh, God. This is when I stop -- start to -- like that. SOBOROFF: Tell us, tell us. MCCARTNEY: It`s the other after the CBE. DREYER: The Next One? MCCARTNEY: Is Next One. JONES: That`s -- so, Next level up, so this week? MCCARTNEY: The Next. I am going up as opposed to going down, which is a good thing. DREYER: So, what is your title then? MCCARTNEY: Don`t ask me. I`m terrible. I am like the worst person in the world. DREYER: Oh, we don`t know. We were talking to America. We don`t know any of this. MCCARTNEY: You can put it out audience. You can have the community search of what I am going to be next. ROKER: Wow. MCCARTNEY: You guys, you can win a Stella McCartney plant-based handbag. How about that? SOBOROFF: Oh, really? MCCARTNEY: If one of you tells us. DREYER: Can I submit an answer? I wouldn`t mind that. MCCARTNEY: You can do it. SOBOROFF: I`ll start Googling. JONES: I know. DREYER: Let`s also talk about your skin care line. This too keeps the environment in mind. I mean, it`s got to be just as hard to do in the skin care industry as well. MCCARTNEY: Oh, God. Yes. It`s really, really tough. You know, there are so many less ingredients, really, when you`re trying work in a sustainable and natural way. But my new skin care range is coming soon. It`s coming here. And I`m so excited. JONES: I can`t wait. MCCARTNEY: I am so proud of it. It took me three years to do. It doesn`t harm animals. It doesn`t harm the planet. It`s refill-based. So, that`s really, really exciting. SOBOROFF: Oh, that`s -- MCCARTNEY: You know, with -- JONES: It`s the way of the future. ROKER: That`s -- everybody is doing that. JONES: Yes. MCCARTNEY: And it`s great. You can throw in your bag. It`s delicious. Like -- and I think the best thing about what I tend to do in luxury fashion and sustainability is you shouldn`t compromise in any way the quality and the luxury element of what you -- you know, you`re investing in. So, the skin care feels like luxurious, it smells delicious and it`s just the results are amazing. DREYER: And yet, your skin is. MCCARTNEY: And yet, it`s learning to nature. DREYER: I`m so close to you right now and your skin is -- MCCARTNEY: Yes. Look at that. Look at that. Smell that. ROKER: OK. That`s not a little creepy. OK. JONES: I love it. headline: Behind The Scenes Of Carrie Underwood`s Epic New Tour
story_text: SHEINELLE JONES: I am excited for this. So, this morning, we have a "TODAY" exclusive. A first look at what to expect when country superstar Carrie Underwood hits the road for her Denim and Rhinestones tour. It`s her first in three years since she took me back stage in South Carolina where it all kicks off. (BEGIN VIDEO CLIP) CARRIE UNDERWOOD, SINGER: It`s a good time. A lot of hard work has gone into the show and very, very proud of it. People are going to have fun. JONES (voiceover): It`s been a few years since a Carrie Underwood tour has made its way across the country. And no one seems more excited than the superstar herself.\\ JONES (on camera): What is the one thing you miss about touring? UNDERWOOD: The crowds. I love to sing. When I`m on stage, I feel like I am at home. And just to feel the energy from people and you look out at all these seats and every single person that is there. JONES (voiceover): The eight-time Grammy winner embarking on a 43-stop arena tour, kicking it all off with a huge show in Greenville, South Carolina. And yours truly is given an all-access pass. JONES (on camera): This gives me like the feels. UNDERWOOD: It`s pretty awesome. It looks bigger. I feel like from up here. JONES: From here? UNDERWOOD: Yes. JONES (voiceover): The stage for her "Denim and Rhinestones" tour lit in dramatic purple will include pyrotechnics and even Carrie performing some high-flying aerial stunts. UNDERWOOD: I am always looking to do things I`ve never have done before. JONES (on camera): Like fly? UNDERWOOD: Like fly. JONES (voiceover): Carrie, taking a page out of her CMT Awards performance. UNDERWOOD: And it`s important to me to make sure like everybody gets a good view. So, we want to figure out some cool ways to get from point A to point B. JONES (on camera): How exciting is that? JONES (voiceover): It`s all part of her goal to bring something new to the arena tours. UNDERWOOD: I want everything to feel different. I don`t want somebody to be like, no, I saw a Carrie Underwood show, you know, four years ago and I`m good. JONES (voiceover): Something definitely worth the price of admission, Carrie`s stunning wardrobe. JONES (on camera): Like this is -- UNDERWOOD: It`s a lot. There`s a lot going. JONES: It`s amazing. Look how beautiful it is. UNDERWOOD: The last part is adding more rhinestones. JONES: I don`t know if you could add any more rhinestones. UNDERWOOD: You always can. I mean -- JONES (voiceover): But something no amount of rhinestones can replace, Carrie`s time with her kids on the tour and at home. [09:35:00] UNDERWOOD: They will be out to visit. This tour, I`m going home a lot more than I ever have before. There is a way to get me home even if it`s just for the day. JONES (on camera): So, are your kids aware of what mommy does? I mean, they`ve been on tour with you before but they are young. UNDERWOOD: I feel like Israel who is seven and a half, he is becoming more aware that it`s not normal, probably because of people around him. So, he`ll go to school and somebody will be, like, I saw your mom on TV last night. JONES (voiceover): One of the Carrie`s few must-haves, a mobile gym. JONES (on camera): This is good. Do you ever work out to your own music? UNDERWOOD: No. JONES: No. UNDERWOOD: It`s weird. JONES (voiceover): A U.S. arena tour, a long way from Carrie`s "American Idol" days. JONES (on camera): Let me take you back. UNDERWOOD: Yes. JONES: It was in 2005. I was a reporter in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and I had the assignment to meet you at the door. The whole town was going nuts because a local girl made it on "American idol." And you walked in and your hands were like -- and I grabbed your hand. I was like, are you ready? If you look at this picture, like this girl right here, do you remember what you were feeling in those early days? UNDERWOOD: At that point, it was all very new, very fresh. And I am, like, OK, you know, let`s enjoy this and have fun and, you know, keep trying to, you know, move forward, but it could all go away at any second. And I think it`s kind of important to treat everything like that, you know, because it just makes you grateful. So, I still -- I`m waiting for the moment where I`m like feeling like I belong. JONES: Are you kidding me? JONES (voiceover): And while I had her, I just had to ask. (MUSIC PLAYING) JONES (on camera): One of your fellow "American Idol" winners, you know, Kelly Clarkson, does her Kellyoke. Have you heard her sing "Before He Cheats?" UNDERWOOD: I have. I have. I feel like she`s one person that you`re like, please, don`t sing my song because you`re going to make me look bad. JONES: Are you joking? You all are both like powerhouses. (END VIDEO CLIP) JONES: That`s funny. I was asking her, you know, if she stays in touch with some of the -- you know, the folks who she, you know, was on "Idol" with years ago. And she has -- great. She says she still talks to Simon, you know, that whole thing. DREYER: Oh, that`s great. JONES: One thing I will say about Carrie is she is so humble and it`s not lost on her. Because I`m like, oh, my god, look at all these clothes and look at all of this. And she is like, yes. You know, she just -- it keeps it -- DREYER: It seems like it hasn`t gone to her head. JONES: Not at all. DREYER: She`s walking around like, can you -- JONES: She is still saying, can you believe it? DREYER: Yes. JONES: I know. DREYER: That`s great. JONES: The tour kicks off tomorrow and tickets are on sale now. There will be pyrotechnics. She flies, as we talked about. She even -- she`s like, I am humble and even -- SOBOROFF: I want to see you get up on the flying thing. JONES: I loved it. Yes. ROKER: Oh, yes. DREYER: With that old hairstyle. JONES: Exactly. DREYER: Yes. JONES: Exactly. DREYER: All right. Coming up, another icon is here with us in studio. She`s -- SOBOROFF: There she is. DREYER: Stella McCartney . You`re going to fashion, family and so much more, right? STELLA MCCARTNEY , FASHION DESIGNER: Absolutely. DREYER: OK. When we come back. SOBOROFF: Don`t go anywhere. JONES: Gorgeous. Gorgeous. SOBOROFF: Nice done. Nice walk off. (COMMERCIAL BREAK) [09:40:00] JONES: We have our life therapist here. She`s also -- SOBOROFF: Really have a good time JONES: -- a fashion royalty with us this morning here in studio. SOBOROFF: Stella McCartney has made a name for herself designing clothes for celebrities like Meghan Markle , Amal Clooney, Beyonce Johnson, so, so many more. DREYER: She launched her brand in 2001, pioneering animal free and ecofriendly fashion. ROKER: And Stella joining us now fresh off her Paris fashion show. JONES: Yes. ROKER: Good morning, Stella. JONES: Good morning. STELLA MCCARTNEY , FASHION DESIGNER: Hi. SOBOROFF: Good to see you. MCCARTNEY: Good morning. ROKER: So, you made this a part of your mission, you know, sustainable ecofriendly. I mean, Bella Hadid`s Met`s dress in the Paris fashion show you making a big splash. How important is that to you and why did you decide so early on? I mean, you were really ahead of the curve on this. MCCARTNEY: You know, I grew up on an organic farm in England as a vegetarian and I basically wanted to be a fashion designer and I was lucky enough to be one and I thought, I can`t compromise my ethics for my career. I don`t want to kill animals. You know, billions of animals get killed for handbags and shoes and leather jackets. So, I was like, I can`t do that. I need to find an alternative. And it started there really. And, you know, the best thing about today is that actually doing sustainable fashion and being ethical and conscious is actually on trend. JONES: It`s in. SOBOROFF: That`s true. MCCARTNEY: Which is a miracle. JONES: Right. DREYER: Is it hard to do? MCCARTNEY: It`s impossible to do. DREYER: Yes. MCCARTNEY: It`s a miracle that I am here today. It`s really, really hard. You know, you have to work with your suppliers so deeply. But it`s this kind of sexiest thing, I think, in fashion. It`s the future of fashion. I think if people don`t start adopting this way of working, then, you know, they`re going to go out of fashion pretty quick. JONES: Yes. SOBOROFF: Thanks in no small part to everything that you have done. And Al mentioned, by the way, at Paris Fashion Week, I want to ask you about that because saw your dad was there, your sister Mary was your photographer. MCCARTNEY: Yes. SOBOROFF: A real family affair. How was it? You guys have a good time? You guys always go together as a group? MCCARTNEY: No. I mean, I`m always there. But, you know, my dad is a busy guy. So, when he can come, I`m always so excited. And, you know, family, the most important thing, right? Let`s face it. Family and friends. And, you know, the fashion industry is a tough cookie and to have your family there supporting you. You know, my family happened to be fabulous. So, it adds a little diamond. SOBOROFF: Understatement. JONES: That`s fair to say. SOBOROFF: I saw -- speaking of your dad, that he posted -- he is almost 80 and he`s doing -- still doing head stands. Here it is. ROKER: Wow. SOBOROFF: Wait. Guys, look in the corner of the TV screen. He is watching MS and there a teaser for our documentary series. So, shout out -- JONES: Oh, look at that, Jacob. SOBOROFF: Shout out to Mr. McCartney. JONES: So, that`s why you -- MCCARTNEY: There you go. SOBOROFF: Do you do that too? MCCARTNEY: I will be sending a check in the post. SOBOROFF: Yes. Thank you very much. MCCARTNEY: And you are going to owe him a couple of pounds. SOBOROFF: Are you a head stander? MCCARTNEY: Yes, I can do the head stand. SOBOROFF: Really? MCCARTNEY: But my dad is very religious about it. He does eye exercises. You know, I mean, he just headlined Glassenbury (ph) a couple of months ago. JONES: Yes. MCCARTNEY: A week after turning 80 to 250,000 people. So, he must be doing something right. JONES: I love it. MCCARTNEY: Should all we do one now? SOBOROFF: No. No, thank you. JONES: You know what, earlier this year you were awarded -- somebody in my ear goes, yes, please. Are you joking? MCCARTNEY: Yes. JONES: Earlier this year you were awarded the CBE. So, it`s the Commander of the Order of the British Empire by the late Queen Elizabeth. MCCARTNEY: I know. SOBOROFF: Amazing. JONES: For your services to fashion and sustainability. Your father, of course, is knighted. And you also designed the dress that Meghan Markle wore at the queen`s funeral? MCCARTNEY: I did. JONES: What an honor. [09:45:00] MCCARTNEY: Yes. Well, you know, it is a real honor, actually. It`s funny. I don`t know. You know, it`s hard to not kind of pinch yourself when these things happen. And yes, I have another award coming up. I`m really excited. I`m -- ROKER: Do tell. SOBOROFF: Tell us about it. MCCARTNEY: It`s the -- oh, God. This is when I stop -- start to -- like that. SOBOROFF: Tell us, tell us. headline: Embattled Republican Senate Candidate Herschel Walker Defiant In The Face Of New Accusations From The Ex-Girlfriend Who Claims He Paid For Her To Have An Abortion
story_text: KRISTEN WELKER: All right, well, now to several new twists and what is arguably the most closely watched Senate race of next month`s midterm elections. Overnight, Georgia`s Republican Senate candidate Herschel Walker , speaking out to NBC News and standing by his claims that he didn`t know an ex-girlfriend had an abortion more than a decade ago. This is the same woman now says Walker wanted her to have a second abortion years later but she refused. NBC`s Allie Raffa is following all of these developments from Atlanta for us this morning, Allie, good morning to you. [07:10:00] ALLIE RAFFA, NBC NEWS CAPITOL HILL CORRESPONDENT: Kristen, good morning. Democrats controlled the Senate by just the thinnest of margins and keeping that hold could easily come down to this crucial Peach State Senate race where in just a few days has gone from too close to call to downright roiled in allegations. (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) RAFFA (voiceover): This morning, all eyes on Georgia, the crucial Senate race between Trump-back to Republican Herschel Walker and incumbent Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock roiled in controversy after bombshell allegations this week by The Daily Beast that Walker paid for a former girlfriend`s abortion in 2009. And a New York Times report Friday that Walker pressured this same woman to have another abortion two years later, but she refused. Walker, who`s running on a staunch anti-abortion platform, repeatedly denying both claims. HERSCHEL WALKER , REPUBLICAN SENATE CANDIDATE, GEORGIA: I`m not going to back down. These things are way, way too high. RAFFA: But in a new twist overnight, the former football star confirming to NBC directly that his wife and the woman making the allegations revealed to be the mother of one of his children, were in contact Friday morning, the woman telling Walker`s wife that he paid for her abortion. Walker sharing copies of the text exchange with NBC News and saying "I`m not saying she did or didn`t have one. I`m saying I don`t know anything about that. I don`t know." Walker telling NBC this was the first time the woman ever mentioned the abortion to him or his wife. But the woman showed the New York Times and The Daily Beast a copy of a receipt from an Atlanta abortion clinic. A check that she claimed was reimbursement for the procedure. And the get well card she claims came from the former football star. We should note we have not seen this documentation. Walker telling NBC News "I don`t remember any card or check or anything. But I was dating her. I could have sent some money. I could have sent a card. But not for the reasons she is saying." Despite the spectacle, most congressional Republicans are still backing Walker. SEN. TED CRUZ, (R-TX): Herschel Walker is going to win that race. This is an effort from Democrats to hold on to power. RAFFA: While state Republicans` frustrations only grow. LT. GOV. GEOFF DUNCAN, (R-GA): Even the most staunch Republicans I think are rattled at the continued flow of information. RAFFA: Just 32 days before voters have their say. (END VIDEOTAPE) RAFFA: As of now, Walker doesn`t have any plans this weekend to meet with voters. But ultimately the choice is theirs. Republicans here tell me they don`t think this controversy will have any impact on this Senate race, while Democrats say this is just another reason they don`t think Walker is fit for Office, Kristen, Peter. WELKER: Allie Raffa, at the center of the political universe right now in Atlanta, thank you. END Content and programming copyright 2022 NBCUniversal. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. headline: Republicans Rally To The Defense Of Georgia Senate Candidate Herschel Walker Facing Devastating Abuse Accusations From His Own Son And A Report He Paid For An Ex-Girlfriend`s Abortion
story_text: HODA KOTB: Meantime, the midterms just over a month away and a firestorm has erupted in a key Senate race in Georgia. Herschel Walker , the former football star now Republican nominee denying a report that he paid for his ex-girlfriend`s abortion. NBC`s Kristen Welker joins us with details on this sordid tale. Hey, Kristen, good morning. KRISTEN WELKER, NBC NEWS CHIEF WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENT: Hi, Hoda, good morning to you. Well, campaigns always brace for the possibility of an October surprise. Well, here it is in the critical Senate race in Georgia with a new controversy surrounding Republican Herschel Walker . Now GOP sources are telling NBC News that leading senators are preparing to stand shoulder to shoulder with him on the airwaves and on the campaign trail. But will it be enough with just five weeks until the midterms? (BEGIN VIDEOTAPE) WELKER (voice-over): This morning Republicans are closing ranks around former football star Herschel Walker , their embattled Senate nominee in Georgia, a swing state that`s critical to Republicans fight to win control of the Senate. After "The Daily Beast" reported Walker in 2009, urged to then girlfriend to get an abortion after he got her pregnant, then reimbursed her for the procedure and sent her a get well card. Walker who says he wants to ban abortion after 15 weeks without exceptions, is denying the allegation. H. WALKER: It is a flat out lie. I can tell you right now, I never asked anyone to get an abortion. I never pay for an abortion. WELKER (voice-over): "The Daily Beast" says the woman asked not to be identified citing privacy concerns, adding she backed up her story by providing the get well card from Walker, an abortion clinic receipt, and a bank receipt with an image of a $700 check signed by Walker. NBC News has not independently verified the documents. CHRISTIAN WALKER, HERSCHEL WALKER`S SON: Everything has been a lie. WELKER (voice-over): Walker is also facing fierce criticism from his own son, Christian, a budding conservative influencer who says the family urged him not to run quote, because we all knew some of his past. C. WALKER: Family values people. He has four kids, four different women, wasn`t in the house raising one of them. He was out having sex with other women. Do care about family values? WELKER (voice-over): Herschel Walker later tweeting, I love my son no matter what. Walker is locked in a tight race with incumbent Democratic senator Raphael Warnock who won a special election by just two percentage points last year. Many Republicans are rushing to Walker`s defense led by former President Trump who`s endorsed him now saying Walker is being slandered and maligned by Democrats. It`s not the first controversy to rock his campaign. He`s falsely claimed he was a member of law enforcement and acknowledged fathering three children out of wedlock. Walker`s ex-wife has accused him of holding a gun to her head and threatening to kill her in incident Walker has blamed on his struggle with mental health. (END VIDEOTAPE) WELKER: Now his challenger again incumbent Democratic senator Raphael Warnock, not directly responding to the controversy. Instead, he`s stressing his long standing support for abortion rights. The big question here, will all of this make a difference? It`s just too soon to tell. But in close races like this one, even a few votes in either direction, could have an impact. Hoda? KOTB: Yes, those are some stunning allegations there. Kristen Welker for us there in Washington. Kristen, thank you. GUTHRIE: Former President Trump has taken his battle over those documents seized at his Florida Country Club, all the way to the Supreme Court filing an emergency request, Mr. Trump asking the court to declare that the 103 classified documents should be reviewed by that independent observer, the special master. Well, the government is arguing that even the special masters should not see those classified documents that were kept at Mar-a- Lago because of national security. The emergency request is being handled by Justice Clarence Thomas , who has given the Department of Justice until Tuesday afternoon to respond.
